(الواو) conjunction; (لا تلبسوا) like «لا تكونوا» in the previous verse, but it is complete (tāmm); (الحقّ) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تلبسوا) , (الواو) conjunction, or the wāw of accompaniment (al-maʿiyya); (تكتموا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), conjoined to «تلبسوا» - or accusative by (أن) concealed after the wāw of accompaniment - «[Note: and the interpreted maṣdar formed from (أنّ) «[Translator's note: so in the source, with shadda; «أن» is meant.]» and the verb is conjoined to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e.: let there not be from you a confounding of the truth with falsehood and a concealing of the truth.]» .. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الحق) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) circumstantial; (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لا تلبسوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the prohibition clause in the previous verse.
The clause «تكتموا..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «تلبسوا».
The clause «أنتم تعلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم) .

* Morphology:
(الباطل) , an active participle of بطل يبطل, of the class of كرم; it is the opposite of الحقّ; its pattern is فاعل.

safi-cedvel:43-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction, (أقيموا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الصلاة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (آتوا) like «أقيموا»; (الزكاة) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, (الواو) conjunction; (اركعوا) like «أقيموا»; (مع) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اركعوا) , (الراكعين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قيموا ... » «[Translator's note: so in the source, for «أقيموا».]» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «لا تلبسوا..» in the previous verse.
The clause «آتوا الزكاة» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أقيموا».
The clause «اركعوا ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause «أقيموا».

* Morphology:
(أقيموا) , in it there is an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion: its origin is أقوموا; it followed the same course as (يقيمون) in verse (3) .
(الصلاة) , a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the four-letter verb صلّى; the alif in it is converted from a wāw, because its plural is صلوات; the wāw came vowelled and what preceded it had fatḥa, so it was converted into alif; its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām.. see verse (3) .
(آتوا) , in it there is an iʿlāl by quiescence and by deletion: its origin is آتيوا with ḍamma on the yāʾ; the ḍamma on the yāʾ was felt heavy, so it was made quiescent - this is iʿlāl by quiescence - then it was deleted because it met, quiescent, with the quiescent wāw - this is iʿlāl by deletion - then the tāʾ was given ḍamma, the vowel of the deleted yāʾ.
(الزكاة) , in it there is an iʿlāl by conversion: the alif is converted from a wāw, as they say زكا يزكو; the wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted into alif. Its pattern is فعلة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām.
(الراكعين) , plural of الراكع, which is an active participle of ركع يركع, of the class of فتح, its pattern فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
- Synecdochic metaphor (al-majāz al-mursal): in the words of Allah the Exalted وَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكاةَ، وَارْكَعُوا مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ, i.e. pray with those who pray; He expressed it by the part, which is bowing (al-rukūʿ), and meant the whole, which is the prayer. So the relation of this figure is partiality (juzʾiyya).

safi-cedvel:44-44.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of disapproval (inkārī); (تأمرون) an imperfect verb, nominative..
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الناس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (بالبرّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأمرون) , (الواو) conjunction; (تنسون) like «تأمرون»; (أنفس) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) circumstantial; (أنتم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (تتلون) like «تأمرون»; (الكتاب) mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الهمزة) for interrogation of reproach and disapproval; (الفاء) conjunction; (لا) negative; (تعقلون) like «تأمرون».
The clause «تأمرون ... » has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تنسون ... » has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أنتم تتلون ... » is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of «تنسون».
The clause «تتلون..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم) .
The clause «تعقلون» has no grammatical position, being (conjoined) to the resumptive clause.

* Morphology:
(البرّ) , a noun for all kinds of good; its verb is برّ يبرّ, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn.
(تنسون) , in it there is an iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion: its origin is تنساون; two quiescent letters met, the alif and the wāw, so the alif was deleted to escape the two quiescent letters, and what precedes the wāw remained with fatḥa as an indication of it; its pattern is تفعون.
(تتلون) , in it there is an iʿlāl by deletion: its origin is تتلوون; two quiescent letters met, the lām of the word and the wāw of the plural; the lām of the word was deleted to escape the meeting of the two quiescent letters; its pattern is تفعون.

* Rhetoric:
- The words of Allah the Exalted وَأَنْتُمْ تَتْلُونَ الْكِتابَ, where He opened the statement with the pronoun for rebuke and greater censure.

safi-cedvel:10-10.t:
* I'rab:
(في قلوب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate), and (هم) is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (مرض) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ). (الفاء) a conjunction. (زاد) past verb, and (هم) is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative. (مرضا) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (الواو) a conjunction. (اللام) a preposition. (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by the lām; the two are attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (عذاب) postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (أليم) naʿt (adjective) of (عذاب), nominative like it. (الباء) a causal preposition. (ما) a maṣdariyya (infinitival) particle [Note: Or a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, with the clause after it as its ṣila (relative clause), and the referent pronoun omitted.]. (كانوا) an incomplete past verb (kāna and its sisters), and (الواو) is an attached pronoun in the position of the nominative as the noun of كان. (يكذبون) imperfect verb, nominative, and (الواو) is a pronoun, the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from (ما) and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, attached to an omitted second naʿt of (عذاب), i.e. "a painful punishment deserved by their being liars".
The clause «في قلوبهم مرض ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and explanatory (istiʾnāfiyya bayāniyya), confirming the meaning of what is said of them: «ما هم بمؤمنين..», or causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «زادهم الله مرضا ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause في قلوبهم مرض.
The clause «لهم عذاب أليم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause زادهم الله مرضا.
The clause «يكذبون ...» is in the position of the accusative as khabar of كانوا, and the clause (كانوا) has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).

* Morphology:
(مرض) a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb مرض بمرض [Translator's note: so printed; read يمرض.], of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(زاد) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its origin is زيد, its imperfect being يزيد. The yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif. It is either an intransitive verb, as in زاد المال (the wealth increased), or a verb transitive to two objects, as in زادك الله جلالا (may Allah increase you in majesty).
(أليم) ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) from ألم يألم, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعيل.
(كانوا) contains iʿlāl by qalb; its origin is كون, its imperfect being يكون. The wāw came vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was converted to alif.

* Rhetoric:
1- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya) in the saying of the Exalted فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ: sickness is borrowed here for what is in their hearts of ignorance, evil belief, enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ and other kinds of unbelief leading to spiritual ruin. The indefiniteness is to indicate its being a vague kind, other than the sicknesses people are familiar with.

safi-cedvel:11-11.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction. (إذا) an adverb (ẓarf) of future time, containing the meaning of condition, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis قالوا. (قيل) past verb, passive. (اللام) a preposition and (الهاء) an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by the lām, attached to (قيل). (لا) prohibitive, making jussive. (تفسدوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the deletion of the nūn; (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent). (في الأرض) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تفسدوا). (قالوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and (الواو) is the fāʿil.
(إنّما) restraining (kāffa) and restrained (makfūfa), having no governing effect. (نحن) a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (مصلحون) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of its nominative is the wāw; the nūn is a compensation for the tanwīn in the singular noun.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «لا تفسدوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: The majority make this clause one with no grammatical position, explicative (mufassira) of the implied nāʾib fāʿil, which is the saying that the clause explains; that is because the clause — in their view — cannot properly be a nāʾib fāʿil, since originally it cannot properly be a fāʿil.. But the clause, from another point of view, is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of the active verb, and when the verb was made passive the clause became nāʾib fāʿil. Some of the early grammarians incline to adopt this view, such as al-Zamakhsharī, who makes the attribution verbal (lafẓī), not semantic, and so do the moderns. A parallel to this verse will come in many noble verses, and we shall parse them as it has been parsed here.].
The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «نحن مصلحون» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying.

* Morphology:
(إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition; it may be free of condition: والليل إذا يغشى; and it may come for surprise (mufājaʾa): خرجت فإذا رجل بالباب (I went out, and lo, a man at the door).
(تفسدوا) contains the deletion of the hamza for lightening, as happened in (يؤمنون, ويقيمون).
(قيل) contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its origin is قول with ḍamma on the first letter and kasra on the second [Translator's note: i.e. قُوِلَ.]. But the wāw — being a weak letter — cannot bear the vowel, so it had to be made vowelless, and its vowel was transferred to the qāf, and it became قول with kasra then sukūn [Translator's note: i.e. قِوْلَ.]. Then the wāw was converted to yāʾ because it is vowelless and preceded by a kasra, and the verb became قيل.
(الأرض) a primitive (jāmid) noun, and the hamza in it is radical; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مصلحون) plural of مصلح, active participle of أصلح. So in it the hamza has been deleted for lightening, as it was deleted from its imperfect, because it is on its pattern, replacing the imperfect prefix with a mīm carrying ḍamma and putting kasra on the letter before the last; its origin is مؤصلحون.

safi-cedvel:12-12.t:
* I'rab:
(ألا) a particle of alerting (tanbīh). (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis (inna and its sisters), and (الهاء) is a pronoun in the position of the accusative as the noun of إنّ, and (الميم) is a particle for the masculine plural. (هم) a detached pronoun [Note: Or a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl), with (المفسدون) as the khabar of إنّ; or a tawkīd (emphasis) of the attached pronoun that is the noun of إنّ, in which case it is borrowed for the position of the accusative.] in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (المفسدون) khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ), and the sign of the nominative is the wāw. (الواو) a conjunction or circumstantial. (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk). (لا) negative. (يشعرون) imperfect, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn; (الواو) is an attached pronoun, the fāʿil (agent).
The clause إنّهم هم المفسدون has no grammatical position, being resumptive (istiʾnāfiyya).
The clause «هم المفسدون» is in the position of the nominative as khabar of إنّ.
The clause «لا يشعرون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause, or it is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun latent in the active participle (المفسدون).

* Morphology:
(المفسدون) plural of المفسد, which is the active participle of أفسد. It contains the deletion of the hamza for lightening, as it was deleted from its imperfect, because it is on its pattern, replacing the imperfect prefix with a mīm carrying ḍamma and putting kasra on the letter before the last; its origin is المؤفسدون.

safi-cedvel:109-109.t:
* I'rab:
(ودّ): past verb. (كثير): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (من أهل): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of كثير. (الكتاب): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (لو): a maṣdar particle. (يردّون): imperfect verb, nominative, the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from (لو) and the verb is in the position of accusative as direct object, its governor being (يودّ). «[Translator's note: so in the source; the verb in the verse is ودّ.]»
(من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يردّون). (إيمان): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) muḍāf ilayhi. (كفارا): a second direct object, its governor being يردّون in the sense of يصيّرون ("they turn [you into]") «[Note: Or a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of يردون; al-ʿUkbarī said this.]». (حسدا): mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb), its governor being يردّون or ودّ. (من عند): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حسدا). (أنفس): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ودّ) «[Note: Or attached to (يردّون).]». (ما): a maṣdar particle. (تبيّن): past verb. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تبيّن). (الحقّ): fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما تبيّن) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء): connective for the apodosis of an implied (muqaddar) condition. (اعفوا): imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الواو): conjunction. (اصفحوا): like اعفوا. (حتّى): a particle of limit and of the genitive. (يأتي): imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) necessarily concealed after حتى. (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (بأمر): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي..) is in the position of genitive by (حتى), attached to (اعفوا واصفحوا).
(إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis. (الله): the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative. (على كلّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to قدير. (شيء): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (قدير): the khabar (predicate) of إنّ, nominative.
The clause «ودّ كثير.»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يردّونكم»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative (لو).
The clause «تبيّن..» الحقّ: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative (ما).
The clause «اعفوا»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e., «if their matter is such, then pardon».
The clause «اصفحوا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اعفوا.
The clause «إن الله ...» قدير: has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya), or a fresh start without causation.

* Morphology:
(كفارا): plural of كافر, the active participle of كفر يكفر, of the pattern-class نصر; its pattern is فاعل (see verse 19). (حسدا): maṣdar of حسد يحسد, of the two pattern-classes نصر and ضرب; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas. There is another maṣdar, حسادة, with fatḥa on the ḥāʾ.
(اعفوا): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion. Its origin is اعفووا with ḍamma on the first wāw; when the ḍamma was felt heavy on the wāw, it was transferred to the fāʾ before it, then the first wāw was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural. Its pattern is افعوا.
(أمره): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of أمر يأمر, of the pattern-class نصر; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

safi-cedvel:110-110.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (أقيموا): imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الصلاة): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو): conjunction. (آتوا): like أقيموا. (الزكاة): direct object, accusative. (الواو): resumptive. (ما): a conditional noun causing the jussive, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object. (تقدّموا): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (لأنفس): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقدّموا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من خير): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ما «[Note: Or a tamyīz (specification) of (ما).]». (تجدوا): imperfect verb, jussive, the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn ... the wāw is the fāʿil, and (الهاء) direct object. (عند): an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (تجدوا) «[Note: It may be a ḥāl of the direct object, i.e., you will find its reward stored up with Allah.]». (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِما تَعْمَلُونَ بَصِيرٌ): the i'rab of its counterpart was given before «[Note: In verse (96) of this sūra.]».. and (ما) is a relative noun, a maṣdar particle, or a described indefinite noun.
The clause «أقيموا ...»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «آتوا ...»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to أقيموا ...
The clause «تقدّموا»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «تجدوه»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis of a jussive condition not joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن الله بصير..»: has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تعملون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the noun-relative or the particle-relative, or it is in the position of genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of (ما).

* Benefits:
1- أقيموا is an imperative verb indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, because its imperfect is one of the five verbs.
There is a rule which says: the imperative verb is made indeclinable on whatever its imperfect is made jussive with.
The gist of this is that the imperative verb is indeclinable on the sukūn if its last letter is sound; it is indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn if it is attached to the alif of the dual, the wāw of the plural or the yāʾ of the addressed feminine; and it is indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter if its last letter is weak.

safi-cedvel:111-111.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (قالوا): past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma,
and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (لن): a particle of negation and the accusative. (يدخل): imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb). (الجنّة): mafʿūl bihi (direct object) «[Note: This is by extension (ʿalā al-saʿa), its origin being "into the Garden".. It may be a direct object in origin.]», accusative. (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (من): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (كان): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (هودا): the khabar (predicate) of كان, accusative. (أو): a conjunction for detailing. (نصارى): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (هودا), accusative like it, the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (تي): a demonstrative, indeclinable on the sukūn appearing on the yāʾ deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) is for distance and (الكاف) for address. (أمانيّ): khabar, nominative (marfūʿ), and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (قل): imperative verb; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (هاتوا): imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil «[Note: In the opinion of Ibn Hishām the verb is inflexible (jāmid), having no past or imperfect.. In the opinion of al-Zamakhsharī it is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and Ibn Hishām rejected that.]». (برهان): direct object, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إن): a conditional particle causing the jussive. (كنتم): an incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) ... and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of كان, in the position of nominative. (صادقين): the khabar of كان, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قالوا ...»: has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: It may be conjoined by the wāw to the clause ودّ كثير.. (verse 109), with what lies between them being parenthetical.]».
The clause «لن يدخل ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «كان هودا»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «تلك أمانيّهم»: has no grammatical position; parenthetical.
The clause «قل ...»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «هاتوا ...»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «إن كنتم صادقين»: has no grammatical position; resumptive ... and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e., «if you are truthful, then bring your proof».

* Morphology:
(هودا): plural of هائد, the active participle of هاد in the sense of "repented". The pattern of هود is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(نصارى): plural of نصران, whose feminine is نصرانه, but it is only used with the yāʾ of relation (nisba). In al-Miṣbāḥ: النصارى is the plural of نصارى. «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "plural of نصراني" is meant.]» The pattern of نصارى is فعالى (see verse 62 of this sūra).
(برهان): a noun meaning "proof"; its pattern is فعلال with ḍamma on the first radical. It is also said that its pattern is فعلان, the nūn in it being augmentative.

* Rhetoric:
It may be said: why was it said «تِلْكَ أَمانِيُّهُمْ» when their saying «لَنْ يَدْخُلَ الْجَنَّةَ» is a single wish?
We say: in that there is a wonderful secret in the craft of eloquence, namely that because of the intensity of their wishing for this wish and its being rooted in their souls, it was put in the plural, as if it were many wishes distributed in every heart, leaving no room for anything else.

* Benefits:
1- تلك أمانيهم: its singular is أمنية, on the pattern «افعولة». It was expressed in the plural because they wish that no good should be sent down upon the believers from their Lord, they wish to turn them back into disbelievers, and they wish that none but themselves should enter the Garden. All of these are false wishes.
2- Concerning البرهان there are two views. One of them is that it is from البرة, its nūn being augmentative, and it is in the sense of cutting and conveys decisive knowledge. The second is that it is from «برهن», from which come البرهنة and البرهان in the sense of clear explanation; on this view its nūn is radical. The soul is at ease with this view, and Allah knows best..

safi-cedvel:112-112.t:
* I'rab:
(بلى): a particle of answer, affirming what they denied. (من): a conditional noun causing the jussive, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (أسلم): past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (وجه): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الله): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أسلم). (الواو): circumstantial. (هو): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (محسن): khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (الفاء): connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (أجر): postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (عند): an adverb of place, accusative, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of أجر. (ربّ): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (لا): negative, non-operative (muhmala) «[Note: Or it operates like ليس, with (خوف) as its noun and (عليهم) as its khabar.]». (خوف): mubtadaʾ, nominative. (على): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted khabar. (الواو): conjunction. (لا): redundant (zāʾida), to emphasize the negation. (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يحزنون): imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «من أسلم..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أسلم وجهه»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of (من) «[Note: The khabar may be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «هو محسن»: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «له أجره»: in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the apodosis of the condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا خوف عليهم»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the apodosis clause.
The clause «لا هم يحزنون»: in the position of jussive, conjoined to the clause لا خوف عليهم.
The clause «يحزنون»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(وجهه): a non-derived (jāmid) noun for the well-known body part ("face"); its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(محسن): active participle of the quadriliteral أحسن; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the second radical.

safi-cedvel:113-113.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (قالت): past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (اليهود): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (ليس): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and (التاء) is for the feminine. (النصارى): the noun of ليس, nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma. (على شيء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of ليس. (الواو): conjunction. (قالت النصارى ليست اليهود على شيء): like its counterpart before it. (الواو): circumstantial. (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (يتلون): imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (الكتاب): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الكاف): a preposition. (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), i.e., «those who do not know said a saying like that». (قال): past verb. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as fāʿil. (لا): negative. (يعلمون): imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (مثل): direct object, its governor being قال, accusative «[Note: Al-ʿUkbarī permitted it to be the direct object of the verb يعلمون.. (مثل) may also be a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, if we make the kāf a noun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, the clause قال being its khabar, with the object implied, i.e., "those who ... said it".]». (قول): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): connective for the apodosis of an implied condition. (الله): the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative. (يحكم): imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (بين): an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (يحكم) by its being made to include the meaning of يفصل ("He decides"), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (يوم): an adverb of time, accusative, attached to (يحكم). (القيامة): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (في): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun in the position of genitive «[Note: It may be a maṣdar particle, with the interpreted maṣdar in the position of genitive.]», attached to (يحكم). (كانوا): incomplete past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the noun of كان. (في): a preposition, and (الهاء) in the position of genitive, attached to (يختلفون), which is an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «قالت اليهود ...»: has no grammatical position, being resumptive or conjoined to the clause قالوا لن يدخل.. «[Note: In verse (111).]».
The clause «ليست النصارى على شيء»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قالت النصارى»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause قالت اليهود.
The clause «ليست اليهود على شيء»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «هم يتلون ...»: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of اليهود and النصارى.
The clause «يتلون ...»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).
The clause «قال الذين ...»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «لا يعلمون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «الله يحكم بينهم»: has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e., «if they differ, then Allah will judge».
The clause «يحكم بينهم»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «كانوا فيه يختلفون»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of (ما), whether the noun-relative or the particle-relative.
The clause «يختلفون»: in the position of accusative as the khabar of كانوا.

* Morphology:
(يتلون): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion. Its origin is يتلوون with ḍamma on the first wāw; then its vowel was transferred to the lām before it, so two quiescent letters met, and the first wāw was deleted to get rid of the two quiescent letters, so it became يتلون. Its pattern is يفعون (see verse 44 of this sūra).

safi-cedvel:114-114.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (من): an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (أظلم): khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ). (من): a preposition. (من): a relative noun «[Note: (من) may be a described indefinite noun, with the clause after it as its naʿt (adjective).]», indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أظلم). (منع): past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is "هو", and it is the referring pronoun. (مساجد): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الله): the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (أن): a maṣdar particle causing the accusative. (يذكر): imperfect verb, passive, accusative. (في): a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يذكر). (اسم): nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) (أن يذكر ...) is in the position of accusative as a second direct object of (منع) «[Note: It may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with a muḍāf deleted, i.e., "for fear that [His name] be mentioned".. or a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) of مساجد, or genitive by an omitted preposition, its implied form being "from [His name] being mentioned", attached to (منع).]». (الواو): conjunction. (سعى): past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (في خراب): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سعى), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (أولاء): a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) a particle of address. (ما): negative. (كان): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb. (اللام): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (أن): like the first. (يدخلوا): imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the deletion of the nūn ... the wāw is the fāʿil, and (ها) a pronoun, direct object. (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (خائفين): ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil of يدخلوها, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يدخلوها) is in the position of nominative as the postponed noun of كان.
The clause «من أظلم..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «منع مساجد»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (من).
The clause «سعى..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منع.. or it is in the position of genitive.
The clause «أولئك ما كان ...»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «ما كان لهم أن يدخلوها»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك).
(اللام): a preposition. (هم): an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar. (في الدنيا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of خزي (a naʿt placed before the noun it describes) «[Note: It may be attached to the omitted khabar.]», the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif. (خزي): postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative. (الواو): conjunction. (لهم في الآخرة عذاب): parsed like its counterpart ... (عظيم): naʿt of عذاب, nominative like it.
The clause «لهم في الدنيا خزي»: has no grammatical position; resumptive «[Note: Or a ḥāl of the pronoun in خائفين, so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl, in the position of accusative.]».
The clause «لهم في الآخرة عذاب»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause, or it is in the position of accusative.

* Morphology:
(أظلم): an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from ظلم; its pattern is أفعل.
(مساجد): plural of مسجد, a noun of place from سجد, of the pattern-class نصر. It came on the pattern مفعل with kasra on the second radical, contrary to the rule, since by rule its second radical should have fatḥa, because its second radical has ḍamma in the imperfect.
(خراب): a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) for التخريب, having fewer letters than the maṣdar; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the first radical.
(خائفي): plural of خائف, the active participle of خاف; the weak letter was converted into a hamza because it came after the alif of فاعل, and this is a regular conversion.

* Benefits:
المسجد: a noun of place on the pattern مفعل; by rights it should have come on the pattern مفعل, by analogy with what has ḍamma on its second radical, but it was heard irregularly, like مغرب and مشرق. «[Translator's note: the source gives the vowelless pattern مفعل twice; the intended contrast is between مفعِل (kasra, as attested) and مفعَل (fatḥa, the rule).]»

safi-cedvel:171-171.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (مثل) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (كفروا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (كمثل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (ينعق) an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), and it is the referent (al-ʿāʾid); (الباء) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (ينعق); (لا) negative; (يسمع) like ينعق; (إلا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (دعاء) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (نداء) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to دعاء by the wāw, accusative like it; (صمّ) khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هم (they), nominative; (بكم) a second khabar, nominative; (عمي) a third khabar, nominative; (الفاء) conjunction, linking the effect to the cause; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negative; (يعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.
And the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «مثل الذين كفروا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ينعق» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذي).
The clause «لا يسمع» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «(هم) صم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هم لا يعقلون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «لا يعقلون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم.

* Morphology:
(دعاء), maṣdar (verbal noun) of دعا يدعو, of the class of نصر. It contains ibdāl (substitution) of the wāw into a hamza; its origin is دعاو: the wāw came at the end of the word after a vowelless alif, so it was converted into a hamza, and this is its rule in every word of this kind.
(نداء), maṣdar of the quadriliteral نادى, and it is a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar. It contains ibdāl of the yāʾ into a hamza: the yāʾ came at the end of the word after a vowelless alif, so it was converted into a hamza, and this is always its rule in every word of this kind.
(صمّ، بكم، عمي), see verse (18) of this sūra.

* Rhetoric:
1- In the verse there is a representative simile (tashbīh tamthīlī): the likeness of those who disbelieve, in what has been mentioned of their absorption in what they are in and their failure to reflect upon the signs cast to them, is like the likeness of the beasts of the one who shouts at them while they hear from him nothing but the ring of the tone and the boom of the voice. It was also said that what is meant is to liken them, in following their forefathers according to the outward appearance of their state while ignorant of its reality, to beasts that hear the voice but do not understand what lies beneath it. So it is the likening of one image to another image.
He likened the disbelievers, when the Messenger calls them, to sheep that are shouted at. It was also said that He likened the caller and the disbeliever to the one shouting and the one shouted at.
2- The explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in likening the disbelievers to the deaf, the dumb and the blind, with the thing likened omitted and the thing it is likened to retained.

safi-cedvel:172-172.t:
* I'rab:
(يأيّها) its i'rab has preceded «[Note: See verse 168 of this sūra.]», (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative as badal (substitute) of أيّ; (آمنوا) a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); (كلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من طيّبات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كلوا) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the object of كلوا, i.e.: eat your provision while it is some of the good things We have provided you.]», (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (رزقنا) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) is the fāʿil, and (كم) is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الواو) conjunction; (اشكروا) like كلوا; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اشكروا); (إن) a jussivizing particle of condition; (كنتم) a defective past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and (تم) is a pronoun, the noun of kāna; (إياه) an overt, detached pronoun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (تعبدون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «كلوا ...» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the vocative (resumptive).
The clause «رزقناكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «اشكروا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause كلوا.
The clause «كنتم.. تعبدون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.. and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: if it is Him you worship, then be grateful to Him.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَاشْكُرُوا لِلَّهِ»: the shift (al-iltifāt) from the first-person pronoun to the third person, to instil awe.
The context of the speech would require Him to say «اشكرونا» (be grateful to Us).
2- Fronting (al-taqdīm): in fronting إياه, to convey exclusivity (al-ikhtiṣāṣ), i.e. be grateful to Him because you single Him out for worship; and your singling Him out for worship indicates that you want a complete worship befitting His grandeur.
3- The verse contains two beautiful concisions by omission (ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf): the omission of the object of كلوا, and the omission of the apodosis of the conditional إن, i.e. فاشكروه (then be grateful to Him); and the omission of the apodosis is common in the speech of the Arabs.

safi-cedvel:173-173.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّما) the restraining (kāffa) and the restrained (makfūfa), having no governing effect; (حرّم) a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), i.e. Allah; (على) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (حرّم); (الميتة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الدم، لحم) two nouns conjoined to الميتة by two conjunctions, accusative like it; (الخنزير) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الواو) conjunction; (ما) a relative noun «[Note: Or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective.. and the clause after it is its naʿt (adjective).]», indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, conjoined to الميتة; (أهلّ) a past verb in the passive; (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) in the position of genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun stand in the place of the fāʿil; (لغير) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أهلّ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الفاء) resumptive; (من) a jussivizing conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اضطرّ) a past verb in the passive, and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (غير) a ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from the nāʾib fāʿil; (باغ) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the deleted yāʾ; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) redundant (zāʾida), to emphasise the negation; (عاد) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to باغ, genitive like it, and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the deleted yāʾ; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا) the lā of generic negation; (إثم) the noun of lā, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (عليه) like عليكم, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of lā; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (غفور) the khabar of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «حرّم عليكم الميتة» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «أهلّ به» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
The clause «من اضطرّ ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اضطرّ ...» is in the position of nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) «[Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be the two clauses of the condition and the apodosis together.]».
The clause «لا إثم عليه» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(الميتة), lightened from الميّتة, the feminine of الميّت, an adjective resembling the active participle (ṣifa mushabbaha). الميتة, in its lightened form, contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion) and iʿlāl by deletion.
Its origin is الميوتة on the pattern فيعلة: the yāʾ and the wāw met in one word with the first of them vowelless, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ, and it became الميّتة with doubling; then the word was lightened by deleting one of the two yāʾs — the ʿayn (second radical) of the word — to indicate the occurrence of death and its completion, and it became الميتة, on the pattern فيلة.
(الدم), a primitive (jāmid) noun whose lām (third radical) — the yāʾ or the wāw — was deleted for no cause, so it contains iʿlāl by deletion. Its dual is دمان or دميان, and some say دموان; its plural is دماء and دميّ, with kasra on the mīm and ḍamma on the dāl.
(الخنزير), the nūn in it is radical according to the verified view, while some consider it augmented, i.e. taken from الخزر, which is narrowness of the eye. The pattern of خنزير is فعليل, with kasra on the fāʾ, and that is on the view that its nūn is radical.
(اضطرّ), it contains the substitution of the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form by a ṭāʾ after the ḍād; its origin is اضترّ. See verse (126) of this sūra.
(باغ), active participle from بغى يبغي, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فاع. It contains iʿlāl by deletion, as the yāʾ was deleted to suit the tanwīn because it is a defective noun (manqūṣ); its origin is الباغي.
(عاد), active participle from عدا يعدو. It contains iʿlāl by qalb and then iʿlāl by deletion. Its origin is العادو, with kasra on the dāl: the letter before the wāw was vowelled with kasra, so the wāw was converted into a yāʾ and it was said العادي; then iʿlāl by deletion took place in it in the same way as in باغ. Its pattern is فاع.
(إثم), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb أثم يأثم, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعل, with kasra on
the fāʾ.
(غفور), a derived adjective whose pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the fāʾ; it is an intensive form of the active participle from غفر يغفر, of the class of ضرب.

* Benefits:
1- His saying, Exalted is He: فَمَنِ اضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ باغٍ وَلا عادٍ فَلا إِثْمَ عَلَيْهِ.
The jurists said that whoever is compelled, out of fear of perishing, may eat of these forbidden things to the extent that stands between him and perishing, and he may not eat a great deal of it.
2- وَما أُهِلَّ بِهِ لِغَيْرِ اللَّهِ: The jurists said: the prohibition on consuming this category of food is confined to the case where we hear that a name other than the name of Allah was mentioned at its slaughter. Accordingly, it is not forbidden to consume food if we do not know what was invoked over it at its slaughter, for example, because the basic rule regarding a slaughtered animal, or any food, is that it is lawful, so long as we do not hear that something other than the name of Allah was mentioned over it, in which case it is forbidden.

safi-cedvel:144-144.t:
* I'rab:
(قد): a particle of frequency (taktīr), i.e. the frequent turning of the Messenger's face «[Note: Or a particle of affirmation (taḥqīq), because the verb is imperfect in form and past in meaning, i.e. "قد رأينا".]». (نرى): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن", for majesty. (تقلّب): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (وجه): muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct), genitive (majrūr), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (في السماء): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تقلّب) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the kāf in وجهك, i.e. "looking into the sky".]». (الفاء): conjunction, linking the effect to the cause. (اللام): the lām of the oath, for an implied oath. (نولّينّ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of nominative; (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, (الكاف) the first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". (قبلة): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ترضى): an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being an implied ḍamma; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi. (الفاء): connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (ولّ): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the weak letter; the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (وجه): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (شطر): an adverb of place, indeclinable on fatḥa, in the position of accusative, attached to (ولّ) «[Note: It may be a second object governed by ولّ, accusative, and it is then declinable.]». (المسجد): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (الحرام): a naʿt (adjective) of المسجد, genitive like it. (الواو): conjunction. (حيثما): a jussive-governing conditional noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, attached to (ولّوا) or to (كنتم) «[Note: Or to the khabar (predicate) of كنتم if it is defective, the noun (ism) of كنتم being the attached pronoun (تم).]», which is a complete (tāmm) past verb in the position of jussive; (تم) is a pronoun, the fāʿil of kāna. (الفاء): connective for the apodosis. (ولوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil. (وجوه): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (شطر): like the first, attached to (ولّوا) «[Note: It may correctly be a second object, and it then becomes declinable.]», and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi.
(الواو): resumptive. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for emphasis. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (أوتوا): a passive past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (الكتاب): mafʿūl bihi. (اللام): it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), for emphasis. (يعلمون): an imperfect verb, nominative; the wāw is the fāʿil. (أنّ): a particle resembling the verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, the noun of anna. (الحقّ): khabar, nominative. (من ربّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of الحقّ. (هم): a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar from أنّ, its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of يعلمون.
(الواو): conjunction. (ما): negative, operating like laysa. (الله): the Name of Majesty, the noun of mā, nominative. (الباء): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (غافل): genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā. (عن): a preposition. (ما): a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to غافل; the referent pronoun is omitted «[Note: (ما) may be a maṣdar-forming particle or an indefinite noun qualified by an adjective.]». (يعملون): an imperfect verb, nominative; the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «نرى ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نولّينّ» has no grammatical position: the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «ترضاها» is in the position of accusative as a naʿt of قبلة.
The clause «ولّ وجهك»: the apodosis of an implied condition.
The clause «كنتم» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the implied conditional clause.
The clause «ولوا وجوهكم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الذين ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أوتوا الكتاب» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين).
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «ما الله بغافل» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «يعملون» has no grammatical position: ṣila of (ما); or it is in the position of genitive as a naʿt of (ما).

* Morphology:
(نرى): it contains deletion of the hamza for lightening; its past is رأى, and by analogy one would say نرأى; the hamza was dropped, then its vowel was transferred to the rāʾ. Its pattern is نفل.. See also verse (55) of this sūra.
(تقلّب): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the five-letter verb تقلّب; its pattern is تفعّل with a fatḥa on the tāʾ and a ḍamma on the doubled ʿayn; it is on the pattern of its past, with a ḍamma on the letter before the last.
(ترضاها): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its original form is ترضي with a yāʾ vowelled with fatḥa: the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif (see verse 120 of this sūra).
(ولّ): it contains iʿlāl by deletion: the lām of the verb was dropped for indeclinability; its pattern is فعّ with a doubled ʿayn bearing kasra.
(شطر): in form it is the maṣdar of the triliteral شطر يشطر of the pattern-class of نصر, but it is used as a noun indicating place; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(الحرام): the maṣdar of حرم يحرم of the pattern-class of فرح and the pattern-class of كرم; it is used as an adjective meaning "the sanctified" (al-muḥarram); its pattern is فعال with a fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Benefits:
1- The gist of the change of the qibla is that the Messenger ﷺ, while in Mecca, used to face Bayt al-Maqdis in his prayer, and when he emigrated to Medina he remained so for a period of sixteen months.
Then he turned during the prayer towards the Kaʿba, and about this He, glory be to Him, says «قَدْ نَرى تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِي السَّماءِ to the end of the verse».

safi-cedvel:145-145.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunction. (اللام): paving the way for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa li-l-qasam). (إن): a jussive-governing conditional particle. (أتى): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (التاء) is an attached pronoun in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (أوتوا): a passive past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (الكتاب): mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb). (بكلّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أتيت). (آية): muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct), genitive (majrūr). (ما): negative. (تبعوا): a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma; the wāw is the fāʿil. (قبلة): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): parenthetical. (ما): negative, operating like laysa. (أنت): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun (ism) of mā. (الباء): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (تابع): genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar (predicate) of mā. (قبلة): mafʿūl bihi of the active participle تابع, accusative, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (ما بعضهم بتابع قبلة بعض): it is parsed like its counterpart above. (الواو): conjunction. (لئن اتّبعت): like لئن أتيت. (أهواء): mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (اتبعت). (ما): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (جاء): a past verb, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", and it is the referent pronoun. (من العلم): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of جاء. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna. (إذا), with nunation or with nūn: a particle of response, with no grammatical position. (اللام): it is the lām of the oath, connecting the answer of the oath with the implied oath. (من الظالمين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of inna, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and the nūn compensating for the nunation.
The clause «إن أتيت» has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause قد نرى in the previous verse.
The clause «أوتوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the relative.
The clause «ما تبعوا ... » has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath implied in ولئن أتيت; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.
The clause «ما أنت بتابع» has no grammatical position: parenthetical.
The clause «ما بعضهم بتابع» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the parenthetical one.
The clause «إن اتبعت» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause إن أتيت.
The clause «جاءك» has no grammatical position: ṣila of (ما).
The clause «إنّك.. من الظالمين» has no grammatical position: the answer to the oath implied in لئن اتبعت; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the answer of the oath.

* Morphology:
(كل): a noun coined for covering all the individuals of a multiple or the totality of the parts of a single thing; it is used only in annexation, overtly or by implication, and its meaning — masculine or feminine, singular, dual or plural — follows what it is annexed to.
(جاء): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by substitution; its original form is جيأ, its imperfect يجيء: the yāʾ was vowelled and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into alif (verse 92).

* Benefits:
وما أنت بتابع قبلتهم: the bāʾ is a redundant preposition that needs no attachment, and تابع is an active participle that has operated as its verb does, putting the word «القبلة» in the accusative. In the verse an oath, a condition and the answer of the oath are combined; the answer of the oath has no grammatical position, and it has made the apodosis unnecessary because it precedes it.

safi-cedvel:146-146.t:
* I'rab:
(الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (آتينا): a past verb, indeclinable on sukūn; (نا) is a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الكاف): a particle of comparison and of the genitive «[Note: Or a noun meaning "مثل", in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is its adjective, i.e. "يعرفونه معرفة مثل معرفة أبنائهم".]». (ما): a maṣdar-forming particle. (يعرفون): like the first. (أبناء): mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما يعرفون) is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq; the implied form is "يعرفونه معرفة — or عرفانا — كمعرفتهم أبناءهم".
(الواو): conjunction. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for emphasis. (فريقا): the noun (ism) of inna, accusative. (من): a preposition, and (هم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فريقا). (اللام): it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), giving emphasis. (يكتمون): like يعرفون. (الحقّ): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو): of the ḥāl (circumstantial). (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ. (يعلمون): like يعرفون.
The clause «الذين آتيناهم ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «أتيناهم الكتاب» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين).
The clause «يعرفونه» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يعرفون أبناءهم» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).
The clause «إنّ فريقا ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive one.
The clause «يكتمون ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar of inna.
The clause «هم يعلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of يكتمون.
The clause «يعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Benefits:
- كما يعرفون أبناءهم: the Arabs used to cite this as a proverb for the strength of knowledge, it being the highest kind of knowledge. Likewise the Jews knew that what the Messenger brought was the truth, but they were disposed by nature to stubborn arrogance and stamped with denial of what the Messenger brought.

safi-cedvel:147-147.t:
* I'rab:
(الحقّ): mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) «[Note: Or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "ما كتموه".. or "الحقّ الذي عليه الرسول".. In that case the preposition and its genitive noun (من ربك) are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الحقّ.]». (من ربّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct). (الفاء): connective for the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition. (لا): prohibitive, jussive-governing. (تكوننّ): an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of jussive (majzūm); (النون) is the nūn of emphasis, and its noun (ism) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (من الممترين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of the defective verb, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «الحقّ من ربّك» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا تكوننّ من الممترين»: the apodosis of an implied condition.

* Morphology:
(الممترين): plural of الممتري, an active participle from the five-letter امترى, meaning "to doubt"; its pattern is مفتعل with a ḍamma on the mīm and a kasra on the ʿayn.

* Benefits:
1- As for the wisdom of the Muslims facing a single qibla: Allah has unified this nation — unified it in its God, its Messenger, its religion and its qibla, unified it despite the difference of homelands, races and languages — and then made this whole unity rest on unity of creed and unity of qibla.
2- Since imtirāʾ is doubt, it does not apply to the Messenger ﷺ; rather it is explained according to the style of the Arabs in address, when speech is directed to the one addressed while someone else is meant.

safi-cedvel:81-81.t:
* I'rab:
(بلى): a particle of answer, affirming a preceding negation, having no grammatical position. (من): a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (كسب): a past verb in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (سيّئة): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (الواو): conjunction. (أحاط): a past verb, and (التاء): for the feminine. (الباء): a preposition, and (الهاء): a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أحاطت), (خطيئة): fāʿil, nominative, and (الهاء): muḍāf ilayhi. (الفاء): connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). (أولاء): a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف): a particle of address. (أصحاب): khabar (predicate), nominative. (النار): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive. (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ. (في): a preposition, and (ها): a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (خالدون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «من كسب.» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «كسب سيّئة» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من) [Note: The khabar may be the protasis and apodosis clauses together.].
The clause «أحاطت به خطيئته» is in the position of nominative, conjoined to the clause كسب..
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ... » is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause هم فيها خالدون is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أولئك) [Note: Or in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أصحاب, the governor in it being the pointing.].

* Morphology:
(سيّئة): feminine of سيئ; it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by conversion. Its origin is سيوئ, on the measure فيعل; its ʿayn is a wāw because it is from ساء يسوء, paradigm نصر.. The yāʾ and the wāw met in the word, the first of them having sukūn, so the wāw was converted to yāʾ and assimilated into the first yāʾ; so it is like صيّب and ميّت. سيئة is a derived adjective.
(خطيئة): a noun meaning "sin"; its pattern is فعيلة, and its verb is خطئ يخطأ, paradigm فرح.

* Rhetoric:
- Explicit metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-taṣrīḥiyya): in His saying, the Exalted, بَلى مَنْ كَسَبَ سَيِّئَةً وَأَحاطَتْ بِهِ خَطِيئَتُهُ فَأُولئِكَ أَصْحابُ النَّارِ هُمْ فِيها خالِدُونَ.
He likened excess in committing sins to a thing that surrounds a thing, the shared quality between them being the impossibility of escape in each of them. This is a most eloquent metaphor, for when a person commits a sin and persists in it, it drives him to commit what is greater than it, and he keeps ascending until a seal is set upon his heart, and he is unable to leave off engaging in it.

safi-cedvel:82-82.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunction. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (آمنوا): a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). (الواو): conjunction. (عملوا): like آمنوا. (الصالحات): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra. (أولئك أصحاب ... ): the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded in the previous verse.
The clause الذين آمنوا ... has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause in the previous [verse].
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «عملوا ... » has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أولئك أصحاب ... » is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of nominative as a second khabar of the mubtadaʾ أولئك [Note: It may be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of أصحاب.. the governor in it being the pointing.].

safi-cedvel:83-83.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunction. (إذ): an adverbial noun in the position of accusative as the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكروا". (أخذنا): a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn.
and (نا): an attached pronoun in the position of nominative, fāʿil (agent). (ميثاق): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (بني): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ, as it is treated like the sound masculine plural. (إسرائيل): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa, since it is barred from tanwīn (a diptote). (لا): negating. (تعبدون): an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (إلّا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (الله): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو): conjunction, (وبالوالدين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, its implied form being "استوصوا" (take good care of). (إحسانا): mafʿūl bihi of the omitted verb.
The following is found in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ of Ibn Ḥayyān [Translator's note: so in the source; the author of al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ is Abū Ḥayyān]:
They differed over what the bāʾ in His saying (بالوالدين) is attached to, and over the accusative of (إحسانا), in several ways:
The first: that (إحسانا) is conjoined to (لا تعبدون), I mean to the maṣdar formed from the maṣdarī particle and the verb, since the implied form according to the one holding this view is "with singling out Allah for worship and with the parents", i.e. "and with dutifulness to the parents" or "with doing good to the parents"; and the accusative of (إحسانا) is as a maṣdar of that omitted muḍāf. The governor in it is the covenant (al-mīthāq), because the preposition-phrase is attached to it, and the "scents of verbs" (rawāʾiḥ al-afʿāl) operate on adverbs and preposition-phrases.
The second: that the preposition is attached to (إحسانا), and (إحسانا) is a maṣdar put in the place of the imperative verb, as though He said "and do good to the parents".. They said: and the bāʾ is synonymous with إلى with this verb; you say أحسنت به and إليه with one meaning. On this construal it may involve the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "and do good with dutifulness to the parents", the meaning being "and do good to the parents by being dutiful to them".. On these two ways, the governor of the preposition-phrase is expressed.
[And Ibn Ḥayyān rejected Ibn ʿAṭiyya's statement that the governor of a maṣdar does not precede it [Translator's note: i.e. that what the maṣdar governs cannot precede it], by saying that this applies to a maṣdar that can be construed as a maṣdarī particle and a verb, not to a maṣdar standing in place of the verb, as occurs in the verse.]
The third: that the governor is omitted, implied as "and do good" or "and they do good to the parents", and (إحسانا) is accusative as a confirming maṣdar of that omitted verb.
The fourth: that the governor is omitted, its implied form being "and take good care of the parents", and (إحسانا) is accusative as the mafʿūl bihi of that omitted verb [and the i'rab of the noble verse has been carried out according to this way].
The fifth: that the governor is omitted, its implied form being "and We enjoined them regarding the parents", and (إحسانا) is accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. "We enjoined them regarding the parents as a kindness from Us", i.e. for the sake of Our kindness.. The verb has come explicitly in His saying, the Exalted:
ووصّينا الإنسان بوالديه حسنا.
Ibn Ḥayyān said: The preferred one is the second way, because there is no implied element in it, and because of the regularity of the maṣdar coming in the sense of the imperative verb.
(الواو): conjunction. (ذي): conjoined to الوالدين, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, since it is one of the five nouns. (القربى): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (اليتامى): conjoined by the wāw to الوالدين, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif. (المساكين): conjoined by the wāw to الوالدين, genitive like it. (الواو): conjunction. (قولوا): an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil. (للناس): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قولوا), (حسنا): a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, being its description, i.e. "a good saying". (الواو): conjunction. (أقيموا): like قولوا. (الصلاة): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (الواو): conjunction. (آتوا): like قولوا. (الزكاة): mafʿūl bihi, accusative. (ثمّ): conjunction. (تولّيتم): a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء): fāʿil, and (الميم): a particle for the masculine plural. (إلّا): a particle of exception. (قليلا): accusative by exception from the nominative pronoun in تولّيتم. (من): a preposition, and (كم): a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (قليلا), (الواو): of the ḥāl (circumstantial). (أنتم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative, mubtadaʾ (subject). (معرضون): khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause أخذنا is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause لا تعبدون إلا الله has no grammatical position: the answer to an oath, because taking the covenant is an oath [Note: The clause is informative (khabariyya) in its wording and performative (inshāʾiyya) in its meaning, because it has the meaning of a prohibition; so it is the maqūl al-qawl (object of saying) of an omitted saying, i.e. "We said: do not worship except Allah"; or the maqūl al-qawl of an omitted ḥāl, i.e. "saying: you shall not worship except Allah".
According to the view of al-ʿUkbarī, the clause may be an accompanying or anticipated ḥāl of the third-person pronoun, i.e. "We took their covenant as professing the oneness [of Allah]"; it is also valid in his view that (أن) is implied before the verb, so the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by a preposition, i.e. "on condition that you do not worship".. or "that you do not worship"; and when أن was omitted, the verb became nominative — but this view is not according to analogy (qiyās).].
The implied clause «استوصوا بالوالدين..» is the maqūl al-qawl of an implied saying, i.e. "We said: take good care of..".
The clause «قولوا..» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the implied clause استوصوا.
The clause «أقيموا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause قولوا.
The clause «آتوا ... » is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause قولوا.
The clause «تولّيتم» has no grammatical position: conjoined to an implied resumption, i.e. "so you accepted that, then you turned away".
The clause «أنتم معرضون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, and it is a confirming ḥāl, because it has the meaning of تولّيتم.

* Morphology:
(إحسانا): a regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb أحسن; its pattern is إفعال, i.e. on the measure of the past with kasra on the first [letter] and an alif added before the last.
(القربى): maṣdar of قرب يقرب, paradigm فرح and paradigm كرم; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(اليتامى): plural of يتيم, a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) of the paradigm ضرب, the paradigm فتح and the paradigm كرم; its pattern is فعيل.. The plural of فعيل on فعالى with fatḥa on the mīm [Translator's note: so in the source; "on the fāʾ" is evidently meant] is rare.
(المساكين): plural of المسكين, a ṣifa mushabbaha from سكن, so the mīm is added; its pattern is مفعيل.
(حسنا): maṣdar of حسن يحسن, paradigm نصر and paradigm كرم; its plural is محاسن, irregularly. Its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn. Ibn Ḥayyān said: it has been said that it may also be an adjective like الحلو and المرّ; so there are الحسن with ḍamma then sukūn and الحسن with two fatḥas, like الحزن and الحزن, and العرب and العرب.
(معرضون): plural of معرض, an active participle from the quadriliteral أعرض, so it is on the measure of its imperfect, by replacing the imperfect prefix [Translator's note: the source has «حرب» for «حرف», a typographical slip] with a mīm with ḍamma and giving kasra to the letter before the last; the hamza has been dropped from its beginning, as it was dropped from its verb in the imperfect.

* Rhetoric:
1- His saying, the Exalted, لا تَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ is a statement in the sense of a prohibition, like His saying, the Exalted, وَلا يُضَارَّ كاتِبٌ وَلا شَهِيدٌ, and as you say "you will go to so-and-so and say such-and-such". It is more eloquent than an explicit prohibition, because it suggests that the one prohibited ought to hasten to refrain from what he was forbidden, so it is as though he has already refrained from it, and the one forbidding reports it.
2- Shift of address (iltifāt): in His saying, the Exalted, ثُمَّ تَوَلَّيْتُمْ; this is a shift to addressing all of the Children of Israel, giving preponderance to their descendants over their forebears, since the mention of all of them had up to then been in the third person.
3- Shift of address (iltifāt): from the third person to the second person in His saying, the Exalted, لا تَعْبُدُونَ.

safi-cedvel:13-13.t:
* I'rab:
(وإذا قيل لهم) its parsing has preceded in verse no. (11). (آمنوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent). (الكاف) a preposition [Note: Or a noun in the sense of مثل (like), in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar because it is its description — or in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from the maṣdar, according to the view of Sībawayh.]. (ما) maṣdariyya (infinitival). (آمن) past verb. (الناس) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) from (ما) and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the kāf, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, i.e. "believe with a belief like the belief of the people".
(قالوا) past verb and its fāʿil. (الهمزة) for the interrogative of disavowal (al-istifhām al-inkārī). (نؤمن) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being نحن (we). (كما آمن السفهاء) is parsed like كما آمن الناس. (ألا إنّهم هم السفهاء ولكن لا يعلمون) is parsed like verse (12), word by word and clause by clause.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The clause «آمنوا ...» is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: See the parsing of the clauses in verse (11), where there is a justification for making the clause nāʾib fāʿil.].
The clause «قالوا» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «نؤمن ...» is in the position of the accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(السفهاء) plural of سفيه, ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle) from the verb سفه يسفه, of the class of فرح; its pattern is فعيل, and the pattern of سفهاء is فعلاء, with ḍamma then fatḥa.

* Rhetoric:
1- We notice in the noble verse the device of variation (al-taghāyur)..
It is in the saying of the Exalted لا يَشْعُرُونَ and the saying of the Exalted لا يَعْلَمُونَ. The detail of that:
The matter of religion, and realising that the believers are upon the truth and the hypocrites upon falsehood, requires reflection and reasoning so that the one reflecting may acquire knowledge. As for hypocrisy and the transgression in it leading to strife and corruption in the land, it is a worldly matter based on customs, known among people, especially among the Arabs in their Jāhiliyya and the mutual support, warfare and partisanship that existed among them; so it is like something perceived by the senses and witnessed. For that reason He said «لا يَشْعُرُونَ» (they do not perceive). And because He mentioned foolishness, which is ignorance, the mention of knowledge with it was a better antithesis (ṭibāq) to it; for that reason He said «لا يَعْلَمُونَ» (they do not know).
2- Allusion (al-kināya): in the saying of the Exalted أَنُؤْمِنُ كَما آمَنَ السُّفَهاءُ.
The Sharīʿa looks at the outward, and with Allah is the knowledge of secrets. For this reason the believers kept silent, and Allah, Glorified is He, answered them about what they concealed. So the speech is an allusion to the perfection of the believers' faith, but in the heart of that allusion there is a jibe; it is in the manner of their saying «اسمع غير مسمع» in admitting both good and evil, and for that reason it was forbidden.
3- In the saying of the Exalted أَنُؤْمِنُ كَما آمَنَ السُّفَهاءُ:
