(جميعا): a noun taken from الجمع, so it is فعيل; it is like a collective noun (ism jamʿ), so it is sometimes treated as a singular, as in the words of the Exalted: نحن جميع منتصر, and sometimes treated as a plural, as in the words of the Exalted: جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنا مُحْضَرُونَ. In its i'rab it may be accusative as a ḥāl, and it may be made to follow what precedes it as tawkīd (emphasis) in the sense of كلّ (see verse 29).
(شديد): a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from شدّ يشدّ of the pattern-class of نصر and the pattern-class of ضرب, and from the second it is more evident; its pattern is فعيل.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَلَوْ يَرَى الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا», i.e. if these «الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا» knew, by the said taking,. The overt noun has been put in the place of the pronoun to indicate that this — taking — «وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَتَّخِذُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ» — is a great wrong (ẓulm).
2- Concision (ījāz): in the verse, by omission of the apodosis of لو; this is frequent and widespread in their speech and occurs often in the Qur'an.

* Benefits:
1- أَشَدُّ حُبًّا: حبّا is parsed as a tamyīz, since every accusative noun after an elative (afʿal al-tafḍīl) is parsed as a tamyīz.
2- The word «دون» is an adverb meaning "beneath", but it comes with other meanings known from the context of speech: it comes meaning "in front of", "behind", "inferior" and "other than", and it mostly occurs in the genitive with «من».

safi-cedvel:206-206.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (إذا) an adverb of future time containing the meaning of condition, in the position of accusative (manṣūb), attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb (أخذته); (قيل) a passive past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the clause اتّق الله, as will come; (اللام) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (قيل); (اتّق) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you); (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (أخذ) past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (العزّة) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (بالإثم) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), either of العزّة, i.e. "bound up with sin", or of the hāʾ that is the object, i.e. "bound up with sin"; the bāʾ may also be causal, in which case the preposition is attached to the verb أخذ, i.e. "pride seized him because of sin". (الفاء) resumptive; (حسب) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (جهنّم) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) occurring in the answer to an omitted oath; (بئس) an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame; (المهاد) the fāʿil of biʾsa, nominative. The one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, and it is جهنّم.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi, and the condition, its protasis and its apodosis are either resumptive or conjoined to the ṣila (relative clause) clause يعجبك [Note: In ayah (204) of this sūra.]. The clause «اتق الله» is in the position of genitive nominative as nāʾib fāʿil [Translator's note: the source reads «في محلّ جرّ رفع»; "in the position of nominative" is evidently meant.] [Note: This is contrary to the opinion of the majority, who hold that the nāʾib fāʿil is implied, i.e. "the saying".. but there is no need for that because the clause is originally the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl) by the verb in the active voice.].
The clause «أخذته العزّة» has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «حسبه جهنّم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «بئس المهاد..» has no grammatical position, being the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(العزّة): maṣdar (verbal noun) of عزّ يعزّ, of the pattern (bāb) ضرب; its wazn is فعلة with kasra then sukūn.
(جهنّم): an underived (jāmid) noun for the abode of punishment; its wazn is فعنّل with fatḥa on the fāʾ and the ʿayn and doubling of the nūn, the second nūn being extra, like علّس [Translator's note: so in the source; the word usually cited is جهنّام / بئر جهنّم.], the one far in depth, and that is why it was so named.
(المهاد): either the plural of مهد, or it is singular meaning "bed".

safi-cedvel:207-207.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (من الناس من يشري) like the i'rab of its counterpart that came before «1»; (نفس) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (ابتغاء) mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative; (مرضاة) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (رؤف) khabar (predicate), nominative; (بالعباد) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) رؤوف.
The clause «من الناس» من يشري is conjoined to the clause من الناس من يقول «2».
The clause «يشري..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «الله رؤف بالعباد» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(نفس): a noun indicating the self, the body or the soul.
It is feminine if the soul is meant, and masculine if the person or the self is meant; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn (see ayah 48 of this sūra).
(ابتغاء): it contains the substitution of hamza for yāʾ because it came at the end after a quiescent alif; its original is ابتغاي, because the verb is ابتغى يبتغي. Its wazn is افتعال, because the substitution changes nothing of the wazn.
(مرضاة): it contains a change (iʿlāl) by substitution; its original is مرضية with fatḥa on the yāʾ, preceded by a ḍād with fatḥa, so the yāʾ was changed to alif to match the vowel of what precedes it, and it became مرضاة; its wazn is مفعلة, and it is a mīm-maṣdar from رضي.

safi-cedvel:208-208.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), an intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative (manṣūb), and (ها) a particle of alerting with no grammatical position; (الذين) badal (substitute) of أيّ, in the position of accusative [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere such a badal is usually said to be in the position of nominative, following the wording of أيّ.]; (آمنوا) past verb, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (ادخلوا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter [Translator's note: so in the source; ادخلوا is indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.], and the wāw is the fāʿil; (في السلم) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ادخلوا); (كافّة) ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (ادخلوا), or ḥāl of السلم, i.e. in all its aspects and laws; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive; (تتّبعوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (خطوات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra in place of the fatḥa, for it is a sound feminine plural; (الشيطان) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of inna; (اللام) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted ḥāl of عدوّ — an adjective placed before what it qualifies; (عدوّ) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (مبين) naʿt (adjective) of عدوّ, nominative like it.
The vocative clause «يأيّها الذين..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «ادخلوا في السلم» has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative (resumptive).
The clause «لا تتّبعوا خطوات» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ادخلوا في السلم.
The clause «إنّه لكم عدو» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(السلم): a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning المسالمة (making peace), or it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the verb سالم; its wazn is فعل with kasra then sukūn, and the fāʾ may take fatḥa; it is treated as masculine and feminine.
(كافّة): a maṣdar meaning "the group" or "all", on the wazn of the active participle from كفّ; it is not annexed and does not take al-, and it is used in the singular, so it is not made dual or plural..

safi-cedvel:209-209.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a conditional particle that makes the verb jussive; (زللتم) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and (تم) is the fāʿil (agent); (من بعد) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (زللتم); (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (جاء) past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (البيّنات) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (ما جاءتكم) is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اعلموا) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of anna, accusative (manṣūb); (عزيز) khabar (predicate), nominative; (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar from (أنّ), its noun and its khabar takes the place of the two objects of اعلموا.
The clause «إن زللتم..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ادخلوا in the previous ayah, because it is within the scope of the vocative.
The clause «جاءتكم البيّنات» has a position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (ما). [Translator's note: The source reads «محلّ لها صلة» ("has a position, ṣila"); by the book's usual pattern «لا محلّ لها» ("has no grammatical position") is intended.]
The clause «اعلموا..» is a causal explanation for the implied apodosis indicated by the content of His saying, the Exalted: إن الله عزيز حكيم, i.e.: "If you slip.. then await His punishment, for Allah is Mighty in His retribution, Wise in His undoing and His settling (of matters)."

* Rhetoric:
1- «فَإِنْ زَلَلْتُمْ», i.e. you turned away from entering «في السلم» and kept aside; its original meaning is falling, and what was mentioned is meant by it figuratively (majāz).

safi-cedvel:210-210.t:
* I'rab:
(هل) an interrogative particle meaning negation, so it indicates a disapproving (inkārī) question; (ينظرون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (يأتي) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and (هم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; in the speech there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the command of Allah comes" or "His punishment".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي) is in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi, i.e.: they await the coming of punishment from Allah.
(في ظلل) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يأتي) or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil; (من الغمام) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of ظلل, or to the verb يأتي, i.e. from the direction of the clouds; (الواو) conjunction; (الملائكة) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, nominative like it. (الواو) resumptive or a conjunction; (قضي) passive past verb; (الأمر) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative; (الواو) resumptive; (إلى الله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ترجع), which is a passive past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; ترجع is an imperfect (muḍāriʿ) verb.]; (الأمور) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative.
The clause «ينظرون» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يأتيهم الله» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أنّ) [Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the ayah is أن.].
The clause «قضي الأمر» has no grammatical position, being resumptive [Note: Or conjoined to the clause يأتيهم الله, with no grammatical position, because it falls within the scope of the awaiting.].
The clause «ترجع الأمور» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(ظلل): plural of ظلّة, a noun for that by means of which one seeks shade; its wazn is فعلة with ḍamma on the fāʾ, and its plural is فعل with ḍamma then fatḥa.
(الغمام): an underived (jāmid) noun for what covers and veils, i.e. clouds; its wazn is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ, and it is the plural of غمامة.
(قضي): the alif was changed to yāʾ because what precedes it takes kasra in the passive.
(الأمر): maṣdar (verbal noun) of أمر يأمر, of the pattern (bāb) نصر; its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «إِلَّا أَنْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ اللَّهُ»: the shift (iltifāt) to the third person in the ayah is to announce that the evil of their deeds requires turning away from them.
2- Metonymic trope (majāz mursal): in His saying, the Exalted, «فِي ظُلَلٍ مِنَ الْغَمامِ», its relationship is causality, because clouds are the likely place of mercy or punishment and their cause: from them the rains pour down, and destructive, sweeping floods may arise.

safi-cedvel:253-253.t:
* I'rab:
(تي) a demonstrative, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn that appears on the yāʾ, which was dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (الرّسل) badal (substitute) of the demonstrative, following it in the nominative, or a naʿt (adjective) of it, or the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; (فضّل) past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, and (نا) the fāʿil (agent); (بعض) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi, and (الميم) for the masculine plural; (على بعض) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (فضلنا); (من) preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar «[Note: It may be attached to an omitted naʿt of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "Some of them are those to whom Allah spoke.." — the relative is then the khabar.]»; (من) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as a postponed mubtadaʾ; (كلّم) past verb.. and the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. كلّمه; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) conjunction; (رفع) like كلّم, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; (بعض) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (درجات) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative «[Note: i.e. "possessors of ranks." Or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because درجة has the meaning of رفعة (raising), i.e. "We raised some of them raisings", i.e. ranks. Or it is accusative by removal of the preposition, the preposition being على, في or إلى. According to Abū Ḥayyān it may be a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), i.e. "and He raised the ranks of some of them above the ranks of others."]»; (الواو) conjunction; آتينا like فضّلنا; (عيسى) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa; (بن) naʿt of عيسى or badal of it, accusative like it; (مريم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and the sign of the genitive is the fatḥa in place of the kasra, because it is a diptote by reason of being a proper name and feminine; (البيّنات) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and the sign of the accusative is the kasra, since it is a sound feminine plural; (الواو) conjunction; (أيّدنا) like فضّلنا, and (الهاء) mafʿūl bihi; (بروح) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb أيّدنا; (القدس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
The clause «تلك الرسل ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «فضّلنا» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ تلك «[Note: Or in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of الرسل.]».
The clause «منهم من كلّم الله» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) «[Note: Or it is a badal of the clause فضّلنا, in the position of a nominative or of an accusative.]».
The clause «كلّم الله» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «رفع..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم من كلّم «[Note: Or in the position of a nominative or an accusative, conjoined to the aforementioned clause.]».
The clause «آتينا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم من كلّم.
The clause «أيّدناه..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause آتينا عيسى ...
(الواو) resumptive; (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (شاء) past verb; (الله the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative «[Translator's note: the closing parenthesis is missing in the source.]», and the object of شاء is omitted, i.e. "had He willed their not differing"; (ما) negative; (اقتتل) past verb; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as fāʿil; (من بعد) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ṣila of the relative, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من بعد) like the first, attached to (اقتتل) «[Note: Or it is a badal of the first (بعدهم), with repetition of the governing word.]»; (ما) a maṣdar-forming particle; (جاء) past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (البيّنات) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما جاءتهم البيّنات) is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
(الواو) conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect; (اختلفوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الفاء) causal; (منهم من آمن) like منهم من كلّم, and likewise (منهم من كفر); (الواو) conjunction; (لو شاء الله ما اقتتلوا) like the first. (الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for rectification; (الله) the Divine Name, the noun of لكن; (يفعل) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (يريد) like يفعل.
The clause «لو شاء الله» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما اقتتل» has no grammatical position: the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «جاءتهم البيّنات» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).
The clause «لكن اختلفوا» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause لو شاء.
The clause «منهم من آمن» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «آمن» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (من).
The clause «منهم من كفر» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause منهم من آمن.
The clause «كفر» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (من).
The clause «لو شاء الله (the second)» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the first clause لو شاء...
The clause «لكنّ الله يفعل» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the second clause لو شاء.
The clause «يفعل» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of لكن.
The clause «يريد» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the relative (ما).

* Morphology:
(الرسل): plural of الرسول, which is one of the intensive forms (ṣiyagh al-mubālagha) but has the meaning of the passive participle, i.e. المرسل (the one sent); its pattern is فعول. (See verse 87.)
(روح): a name for that by which a created being has life; it is treated as masculine and feminine; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn (see verse 87).

* Benefits:
1- «وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَهُمْ دَرَجاتٍ», i.e. "and among them is one whom He raised above all the other prophets."
What is apparent is that He meant Muhammad ﷺ, since he is the one preferred over them, in that he was given what no one else was given of numerous signs, rising to a thousand signs or more. And in this vagueness there is, as is evident, a magnification of his merit and an elevation of his rank, since it bears witness that he is the well-known figure who cannot be confused with another, the distinguished one who cannot be mistaken.

safi-cedvel:276-276.t:
* I'rab:
(يمحق) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (الربا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif; (الواو) conjunction; (يربي) like يمحق, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and the agent is "huwa" (he); (الصدقات) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الواو) conjunction; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (لا) negative; (يحبّ) like يمحق, and the agent is "huwa"; (كلّ) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (كفّار) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (أثيم) naʿt (adjective) of كفّار, genitive like it.
The clause «يمحق الله الربا» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يربي الصدقات» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «الله لا يحب ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «لا يحبّ كلّ كفّار» is in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(كفّار): an intensive form of the active participle from the verb كفر يكفر, of the نصر pattern; its wazn is فعّال.
(أثيم): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) on the wazn فعيل, from the verb أثم يأثم, of the فرح pattern.

safi-cedvel:277-277.t:
* I'rab:
(إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of an accusative as the noun of إنّ; (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الواو) conjunction; (عملوا) like آمنوا; (الصالحات) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra; (الواو) conjunction; (أقاموا الصلاة- آتوا الزكاة) like عملوا الصالحات; (لهم أجرهم عند ربّهم ولا خوف عليهم ولا هم يحزنون) its i'rab has been given before «[Note: in ayah (262) of this sūra.]».
The clause «إنّ الذين آمنوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «عملوا الصالحات» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «أقاموا الصلاة» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «آتوا الزكاة» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «لهم أجرهم» is in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «لا خوف عليهم» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لهم أجرهم.
The clause «هم يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause لا خوف عليهم.
The clause «يحزنون» is in the position of a nominative as khabar of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

* Morphology:
(أقاموا): it contains iʿlāl by substitution (qalb): the ʿayn of the verb, the wāw, was changed to an alif because it came after a fatḥa; its original form is أقوموا. The vowel of the wāw was moved to the qāf before it (iʿlāl by vowel-removal, taskīn), then the wāw was changed to an alif (see ayah 177 of this sūra).
(آتوا): the word contains iʿlāl by deletion: the alif, the lām of the word, was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw was given a fatḥa to indicate it; its wazn is أفعوا, with fatḥa on the hamza and the ʿayn. The madda at the beginning of the word is originally two hamzas, the first voweled and the second quiescent, i.e. أأتوا ... (see ayah 43 of this sūra).

safi-cedvel:278-278.t:
* I'rab:
(يا) a vocative particle; (أيّ) the one addressed (munādā), a definite-intended indefinite (nakira maqṣūda), indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of an accusative; and (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as badal (substitute) of أيّ, or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or naʿt (adjective); (آمنوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) conjunction; (ذروا) like اتّقوا; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (بقي) a past verb, and the agent is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (it), and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (من الربا) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of بقي; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كنتم) a defective past verb (of kāna and its sisters), indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive; and (تم) is the noun of كان; (مؤمنين) its khabar (predicate), accusative, the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «أيّها الذين ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (الذين).
The clause «اتّقوا الله» has no grammatical position; it is the response to the vocative.
The clause «ذروا ...» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the response to the vocative.
The clause «بقي» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «إن كنتم مؤمنين» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech, i.e.: fear Allah and give up what remains of usury.

* Morphology:
(ذروا): it contains iʿlāl by deletion: the fāʾ of the word, which is the wāw, was deleted from it in the imperfect and the imperative; its wazn is علوا, with fatḥa on the ʿayn.

safi-cedvel:279-279.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (لم) a negative particle; (تفعلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) «[Note: We have chosen in the i'rab that the verb be governed by (إن); as for (لم), its effect is negation and nothing else ("ليس عير" in the text) [Translator's note: "عير" appears to be a misprint for "غير"], contrary to the view of the majority; this is so that the condition retains its future character.]», the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (ائذنوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (بحرب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ائذنوا); (من الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to a naʿt (adjective) of حرب; (الواو) conjunction; (رسول) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the Name of Majesty, genitive like it, and (الهاء) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (الواو) conjunction; (إن) like the first; (تبتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of a jussive, and (تم) is the fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (رؤوس) a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (أموال) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (لا) negative; (تظلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) negative; (تظلمون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The clause «لم تفعلوا» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause اتّقوا الله in the preceding ayah.
The clause «ائذنوا ...» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «إن تبتم» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن لم تفعلوا.
The clause «لكم رؤوس أموالكم» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «لا تظلمون» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) of the genitive pronoun in لكم «[Note: It is permissible for the clause to be resumptive, with no grammatical position.]». The clause «لا تظلمون» [Translator's note: i.e. the second one, لا تُظلمون] is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause لا تظلمون, or has no grammatical position.

* Morphology:
(فأذنوا): in it the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) is deleted because the fāʾ comes before it and because there is a hamza after the connecting hamza; likewise if the connecting hamza is preceded by the wāw, it is deleted.
(بحرب): a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from the quadriliteral حارب; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn. It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb حرب يحرب الرجل, of the نصر pattern, meaning "he robbed him of his property".
(تبتم): it contains iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is توبتم with a voweled wāw, then the wāw was made quiescent for lightness, then it was deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, then the tāʾ was given a ḍamma to indicate the deleted letter.
(رؤوس): plural of رأس, an underived (jāmid) noun; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn. The use of "head" here is figurative, and its meaning is "the principal".

safi-cedvel:280-280.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (إن) a jussive conditional particle; (كان) a complete (tāmm) past verb «[Note: Or it is defective (nāqiṣ), with its khabar omitted, its implied form being "a debtor" (غريما) or "you have a claim against him" (لكم عليه حقّ).]», indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (ذو) fāʿil (agent), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, since it is one of the five nouns; (عسرة) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (نظرة) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "the obligation" (الواجب) «[Note: Or it is a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted and fronted, i.e. "then upon you is a postponement until ease" (فعليكم نظرة إلى ميسرة).]»; (إلى ميسرة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) نظرة, with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "until the time of ease"; (الواو) resumptive; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تصدّقوا) an imperfect verb, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; one of the two tāʾs has been deleted from the verb; (خير) khabar of the mubtadaʾ formed from the interpreted maṣdar; (اللام) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خير) or to a naʿt (adjective) of it.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تصدّقوا) is in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, i.e.: "your giving charity is better for you".
(إن كنتم) its i'rab has been given before «[Note: in ayah (278) of this sūra.]»; (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «إن كان ذو عسرة» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause إن لم تفعلوا.
The clause «(الواجب) نظرة» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «أن تصدّقوا خير» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «إن كنتم تعلمون» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of an accusative as khabar of كنتم. The apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: if you know the merit of giving charity, then your giving charity is better for you.

* Morphology:
(عسرة): maṣdar of عسر يعسر, of the فرح pattern and the كرم pattern; the tāʾ in it is additional.
(نظرة): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar from نظر فلانا الدين — of the نصر pattern — i.e. he granted him a delay; or it is a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) from أنظر فلانا الدين.
(ميسرة): a mīmī maṣdar from the verb يسر, and the tāʾ is additional.
(تصدّقوا): it contains a deleted tāʾ; its original form is تتصدّقوا.

safi-cedvel:281-281.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive — or conjunction —; (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn — and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (يوما) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (ترجعون) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (في) a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترجعون); (إلى الله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ترجعون); (ثمّ) a conjunction; (توفّى) a passive imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif; and (كلّ) nāʾib fāʿil, nominative; (نفس) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive; (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (كسب) a past verb, and (التاء) is the tāʾ of the feminine, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "هي" (she); the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. كسبته; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (لا) negative; (يظلمون) like ترجعون.
The clause «اتّقوا يوما» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive «[Note: Or conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause.]».
The clause «ترجعون فيه» is in the position of an accusative as naʿt (adjective) of (يوما).
The clause «توفّى كلّ نفس» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause ترجعون, and the linking pronoun is implied, i.e. توفّى فيه.
The clause «كسبت» has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «هم لا يظلمون» is in the position of an accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «لا يظلمون» is in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (هم).

safi-cedvel:24-24.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) a conjunction. (إن) a jussive conditional particle. (لم) a particle of negation, conversion (qalb) and apocopation (jazm). (تفعلوا) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) [Note: The majority make (لم), not (إن), the one that puts it in the jussive, because the former is stronger in governing. But nothing prevents us from making (إن) the governing word, so that the verb is confined to the future and remains so; because when the verb is made jussive by (لم), its meaning is converted to the past, and this undermines the sense of the condition.], and (الواو) is the fāʿil (agent). (الواو) parenthetical. (لن) a particle of negation and of the subjunctive (naṣb). (تفعلوا) imperfect, subjunctive (manṣūb), and the sign of the subjunctive is the deletion of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (الفاء) linking the apodosis of the condition. (اتقوا) imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn, and (الواو) is the fāʿil. (النار) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative. (التي) relative noun in the position of the accusative as naʿt (adjective) of (النار). (وقود) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (ها) is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). (الناس) khabar (predicate), nominative. (الحجارة) conjoined by the wāw to الناس, nominative like it. (أعد) past verb, passive, and (التاء) is for the feminine; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being هي, i.e. the Fire. (للكافرين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أعدّت).
The clause «لم تفعلوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to a preceding resumptive clause.
The clause «لن تفعلوا» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical (iʿtirāḍiyya).
The clause «اتّقوا النار» is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «وقودها النار» [Translator's note: so printed; the clause is وقودها الناس.] has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (التي).
The clause «أعدت..» is in the position of the accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial) from النار [Note: It may be resumptive, with no grammatical position.].

* Morphology:
(اتّقوا) contains ibdāl (substitution) as in the verb (تتّقون); see verse (21).
(وقود) a primitive (jāmid) noun for that with which fire is kindled; its pattern is فعول with fatḥa on the wāw.. The maṣdar (verbal noun) from it is on the pattern فعول with ḍamma on the fāʾ. Some of them said that both fatḥa and ḍamma are valid in the noun and the maṣdar: that with which fire is kindled is called وقود with fatḥa and with ḍamma, and likewise its kindling; and the like is said of الوضوء and السحور.. But what has come in the verse is the more eloquent.

* Rhetoric:
1- Allusion (al-kināya): in the saying of the Exalted فَاتَّقُوا النَّارَ..
Guarding against the Fire is an allusion to guarding against obstinacy, since by that its being caused by it and its resulting from it are realised. It is as if it were said: "Since you are unable to bring the like of it, as is established, guard against denying that it was sent down from Allah, Glorified is He, for that deserves punishment by the Fire." But the said allusion was preferred to that, based on depicting obstinacy in the form of the Fire and making being characterised by it the very contact with the Fire, for exaggeration in making its matter dreadful and its affair hideous, and to show the perfect concern for warning those addressed against it, repelling them from it and urging them to earnestness in realising what is alluded to. And in it there is a marvellous concision that is not hidden.
2- Parenthesis (al-iʿtirāḍ): in the saying of the Exalted وَلَنْ تَفْعَلُوا..
The clause is a parenthesis between the two parts of the conditional sentence, confirming the content of its first part and emphasising the obligation of acting upon its second part. This is a dazzling miracle, since He informed of the unseen whose knowledge is exclusive to Him, Mighty and Majestic is He.

* Benefits:
Several verses have come in the Noble Qur'an carrying the spirit of challenge and of demonstrating the inability of the polytheists to imitate the Qur'an, copy it, or bring a single sūra like its surahs; and Quraysh stood helpless and surrendering before this challenge. History tells us of a few people who tried to imitate the Noble Qur'an and produced what was a witness to their inability and a mark of shame and silliness on the tongues of those pretenders to prophethood, among whom were Musaylima the Liar, al-Aswad al-ʿAnsī and Sajāḥ, and among them al-Mutanabbī in his youth. And there are those who falsely related that about al-Maʿarrī in his book «al-Fuṣūl wa-l-Ghāyāt».
All the verifying and fair-minded scholars have denied that of al-Maʿarrī.
Among what history has preserved for us of the «Qur'an» of Musaylima is his saying: «يا ضفدع يا ضفدعين، نقّي كما تنقين نصفك في الماء ونصفك في الطين، لا الماء تكدرين، ولا الشارب تمنعين» (O frog, daughter of two frogs, croak as you croak; half of you in the water and half of you in the mud; you neither muddy the water nor keep away the drinker).
Some people claimed that Ibn al-Muqaffaʿ tried to imitate the Qur'an, and when the style of the Qur'an astounded him, he burned what he had written. And thus the challenge remains standing until the Day of Resurrection.

safi-cedvel:128-128.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا): its i'rab was given in the previous verse. (الواو): conjunction. (اجعل): an imperative verb of supplication; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت", and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (مسلمين): a second direct object, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, as it is a dual. (اللام): a preposition, and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مسلمين), i.e., «submissive». (الواو): conjunction. (من ذرّيّة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being اجعل, and (نا) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (أمّة): direct object, accusative, of the omitted verb. (مسلمة): naʿt (adjective) of أمة, accusative like it. (لك): like the first, attached to مسلمة. (الواو): conjunction. (أرنا): like اجعلنا. (مناسك): a second direct object, accusative, and (نا) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (تب): like اجعل. (على): a preposition, and (نا) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تب). (إنّك أنت التّواب الرحيم): like its counterpart in the previous verse.
The vocative clause «ربّنا..»: has no grammatical position; parenthetical, for imploring mercy.
The clause «اجعلنا..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تقبّل منا in the previous verse.
The clause «(اجعل) من ذرّيّتنا»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اجعلنا.
The clause «أرنا..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اجعلنا.
The clause «تب علينا..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اجعلنا.
The clause «إنّك أنت التوّاب»: has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(مسلمين): dual of مسلم, the active participle of the quadriliteral أسلم; its pattern is مفعل, with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the second radical.
(أمّة): a noun for a community; its pattern is فعلة with ḍamma on the first radical, its second and third radicals being identical.
(أرنا): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by deletion to suit the indeclinable form: its third radical, a weak letter, was deleted. It also contains the deletion of the hamza for lightness; its origin is أرئينا.. Its pattern is أفنا.
(مناسك): plural of منسك, a noun of place from نسك ينسك, of the pattern-class نصر; its pattern is مفعل with fatḥa on the second radical.. The second radical may take kasra, contrary to the rule.

safi-cedvel:129-129.t:
* I'rab:
(ربّنا): its i'rab was given (verse 127), and it was repeated to emphasize the imploring of mercy. (وابعث): like واجعل (verse 128). (في): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ابعث). (رسولا): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (من): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (رسولا). (يتلو): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the wāw; the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (عليهم): like فيهم, attached to (يتلو). (آيات): direct object, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (يعلّم): imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is "هو", and (هم) an attached pronoun, direct object. (الكتاب): a second direct object, accusative. (الحكمة): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الكتاب by the wāw, accusative like it. (الواو): conjunction. (يزكّيهم): like يعلّمهم. (إنّك أنت العزيز الحكيم): like إنّك أنت السميع العليم «[Note: In verse (127).]».
The vocative clause «ربّنا..»: has no grammatical position; parenthetical, imploring mercy.
The clause «ابعث فيهم..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause اجعلنا مسلمين «[Note: In verse (128).]».
The clause «يتلو عليهم»: in the position of accusative as a naʿt of (رسولا) «[Note: It may be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of (رسولا), since it is described.]».
The clause «يعلّمهم..»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «يزكّيهم..»: in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause يتلو.
The clause «إنّك أنت العزيز»: has no grammatical position; causal (taʿlīliyya).

* Morphology:
(الحكمة): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb حكم يحكم, of the pattern-class كرم, i.e., "he became wise"; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra on the first radical and sukūn on the second.
(العزيز): an adjective resembling the participle (ṣifa mushabbaha) from عزّ يعزّ, of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فعيل.

safi-cedvel:130-130.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (من): an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); it includes the meaning of negation and disapproval. (يرغب): imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (عن ملّة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يرغب). (إبراهيم): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa. (إلا): a particle of exception. (من): a relative noun «[Note: Or a described indefinite noun, with the clause after it as its naʿt (adjective).]» in the position of nominative as badal (substitute) of the fāʿil of يرغب «[Note: Or in the position of accusative as the excepted (mustathnā).]». (سفه): past verb, and the fāʿil is "هو". (نفس): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): resumptive. (اللام): occurring in the answer to an implied (muqaddar) oath. (قد): a particle of realization. (اصطفينا): past verb with its fāʿil, and (الهاء) a pronoun, direct object. (في الدنيا): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the hāʾ, the sign of the genitive being the kasra implied on the alif. (الواو): conjunction. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun, the noun of أنّ. «[Translator's note: so in the source; the particle in the verse is إنّ.]» (في الآخرة): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to الصالحين. (اللام): the lām of oath, conveying emphasis «[Note: Or it is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa).]». (من الصالحين): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ.
The clause «من يرغب..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «يرغب عن ملّة..»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «سفه..»: has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
The clause «اصطفيناه..»: has no grammatical position, being the answer to an implied oath.
The clause «إنّه في الآخرة..»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the answer to the oath.

* Morphology:
(اصطفيناه): it contains the substitution (ibdāl) of the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form with ṭāʾ because it came after the ṣād; its origin is اصتفيناه. It also contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion: the alif was converted into a yāʾ — because it is the fourth letter — when the verb was attributed to the pronoun of the speaker.

* Benefits:
1- The verb «رغب» has two different meanings. The first is "to want it and love it": «رغب فيه» and «رغب به». The second is "to dislike a thing and renounce it", and its example is «رغب عنه» and «رغب عن ملة إبراهيم».

safi-cedvel:131-131.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ): an adverb of past time; it may be purely adverbial and so attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اصطفيناه) in the previous verse, or it is mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being اذكر ("remember"). (قال): past verb. (اللام): a preposition, attached to (قال), and (الهاء) is in the position of genitive by the lām. (ربّ): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (أسلم): imperative verb; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت". (قال): like the first. (أسلمت): past verb with its fāʿil. (لربّ): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أسلمت). (العالمين): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «قال له ربّه..»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أسلم»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قال..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «أسلمت..»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech.

* Benefits:
1- إذ قال له ربه: the clause «قال» is in the position of genitive by annexation, because it occurs after the adverb «إذ».
2- In this verse we find the command to submit (islām) given by Allah to the father of the prophets, Abraham, and he responded to the command of his Lord. Then we find this passed on among the prophets of the Children of Israel: Abraham enjoined it upon his sons, as Jacob enjoined it upon his sons: يا بَنِيَّ إِنَّ اللَّهَ اصْطَفى لَكُمُ الدِّينَ فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ. And He, glory be to Him, says in this context: أَمْ كُنْتُمْ شُهَداءَ إِذْ حَضَرَ يَعْقُوبَ الْمَوْتُ إِذْ قالَ لِبَنِيهِ ما تَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ بَعْدِي قالُوا نَعْبُدُ إِلهَكَ وَإِلهَ آبائِكَ إِبْراهِيمَ وَإِسْماعِيلَ وَإِسْحاقَ إِلهاً واحِداً وَنَحْنُ لَهُ مُسْلِمُونَ.
We find this meaning repeated on the tongues of many prophets, which leads us to say that the true religion is one religion and that Islam was the religion of all the prophets. If people stripped themselves of their desires, they would meet on one ground: the one truth, and the right that is not multiple.
3- We know that the sound masculine plural is inflected with the wāw in the nominative and the yāʾ in the accusative and genitive, and that it has conditions. If a noun lacks some of its conditions and is inflected with the same inflection, we call it "attached to the sound masculine plural" (mulḥaq). The nouns attached to it are limited in number, namely: عالمون, عليون, وابلون, راضون, بنون, سنون, أهلون, ذوو, عضون, and عشرون to تسعين. The definition of the attached noun is: every triliteral noun whose third radical has been replaced by the hāʾ of the feminine, such as عضة → عضين, عزة → عزين, ثبة → ثبين, مائة → مائتين, ظبة → ظبين, and the like.
4- The Arabic language inclines towards lightness and ease of pronunciation. The scholars of grammar and language have found many examples that achieve this aim and support this tendency. Among them is the repetition of one letter, from which difficulty of pronunciation may arise, such as the succession of tāʾs at the beginning of some imperfect verbs; and the meeting of two quiescent letters, and the adjacency of letters close in their points of articulation. In these cases and those similar to them, the word is lightened by means of deletion, substitution or assimilation. The scope of this book does not allow for this topic, so whoever wishes may consult it in the books of philology and the like.

safi-cedvel:132-132.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): resumptive. (وصّى): past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif. (الباء): a preposition, and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (وصّى). (إبراهيم): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (بني): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the yāʾ, since it is attached to the sound masculine plural, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi. (الواو): conjunction. (يعقوب): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to إبراهيم, nominative like it. (يا): vocative particle. (بنيّ): the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.. and the second (الياء) is an attached pronoun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. (إنّ): a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis. (الله): the Name of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative. (اصطفى): past verb, indeclinable on the implied fatḥa; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو". (اللام): a preposition, and (كم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to the verb اصطفى. (الدين): direct object, accusative. (الفاء): conjunction, linking the effect to the cause «[Note: Or connective for the apodosis of an implied condition, the clause being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e., "if the matter is such, then do not die except.."]». (لا): prohibitive, causing the jussive. (تموتنّ): imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, since it is one of the five verbs; the wāw, deleted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, is the fāʿil.. and (النون) is the heavy nūn of emphasis. (إلا): a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). (الواو): circumstantial. (أنتم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (مسلمون): khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «وصّى بها إبراهيم..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The vocative clause «and its response..»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl) of the omitted verb قال «[Note: According to some it is explicative of the verb of enjoining.]».
The clause «إنّ الله اصطفى»: has no grammatical position, being the response to the vocative.
The clause «اصطفى لكم..»: in the position of nominative as the khabar of (إنّ).
The clause «لا تموتنّ»: has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause that is the response to the vocative.
The clause «أنتم مسلمون»: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

* Morphology:
(وصّى): it contains a weak-letter change (iʿlāl) by conversion. Its origin is وصّي, because the maṣdar of its bare form is وصاية; when the yāʾ came voweled after a fatḥa, it was converted into an alif. Its pattern is فعّل.
(اصطفى): it contains substitution (ibdāl) and iʿlāl, as in the previous verse (130). (تموتنّ): the wāw of the plural was deleted from it because it came quiescent before the heavy nūn of emphasis; its origin is تموتونّ. The first nūn of the nūn of emphasis is quiescent, in keeping with the doubling, and for this reason the wāw of the plural was deleted.

* Rhetoric:
In the saying of Allah the Exalted فَلا تَمُوتُنَّ إِلَّا وَأَنْتُمْ مُسْلِمُونَ there is a splendid rhetorical subtlety.
Death is not within a person's power, such that it could be forbidden. Rather, in reality the prohibition is only against their not being Muslims at the time of their death. It is like your saying: "Do not pray except while you are humble", since the prohibition in it is only against abandoning humility while praying, not against prayer.
The subtlety in expressing it this way is to show that their dying not upon Islam is a death in which there is no good, and that prayer in which there is no humility is like «no prayer».

safi-cedvel:133-133.t:
* I'rab:
(أم): disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), in the sense of بل and the hamza, and it conveys beginning «[Note: Al-Zamakhsharī permitted it to be connected (muttaṣila), with what it is conjoined to being omitted, i.e., "Do you claim Judaism for the prophets, or were you witnesses?"]». (كنتم): an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and (تم) a pronoun, the noun of كان. (شهداء): the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, accusative (manṣūb), barred from nunation because it is on the pattern فعلاء. (إذ): an adverb of past time, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) شهداء. (حضر): past verb. (يعقوب): fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, barred from nunation on account of being a proper name and foreign. (الموت): fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ). (إذ): an adverb, badal (substitute) of the first adverb, in the position of accusative. (قال): past verb, and the fāʿil is "هو". (لبني): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قال), the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (ما): an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a fronted direct object. (تعبدون): imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (من بعد): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تعبدون), and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (قالوا): past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil. (نعبد): imperfect verb, nominative; the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن". (إله): direct object, accusative, and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إله): maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first by the wāw, accusative like it. (آباء): muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi. (إبراهيم): badal of آباء, genitive like it, the sign of the genitive being the fatḥa because it is a diptote. (إسماعيل وإسحاق): two nouns conjoined to إبراهيم by the two conjunctions, genitive like it. (إلها): badal of the first إله, accusative like it «[Note: It may be accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), even though it is non-derived (jāmid), because it is described.]». (واحدا): naʿt (adjective) of إله, accusative like it. (الواو): circumstantial. (نحن): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). (اللام): a preposition, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (مسلمون), which is the khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw.
The clause «كنتم شهداء..»: has no grammatical position; resumptive.
The clause «حضر.. الموت»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قال لبنيه..»: in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ما تعبدون..»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «قالوا.»: has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «نعبد..»: in the position of accusative as the object of speech.
The clause «نحن له مسلمون»: in the position of accusative as a ḥāl «[Note: The wāw may be a conjunction, with the clause conjoined to the object-of-speech clause نعبد.]».

* Morphology:
(شهداء): plural of شاهد, the active participle of شهد يشهد, of the pattern-class فرح; its pattern is فاعل, and the pattern of شهداء is فعلاء (verse 23).
(آباء): the madda in it is formed from two hamzas, the first with fatḥa and the second quiescent; its origin is أأباء. Then the two alifs were merged and a madda placed over them. The final hamza is converted from a wāw (آباو); when it came at the end after a quiescent alif, it was converted into a hamza, so it became آباء. Its pattern is أفعال.
(يعقوب): it is said he was so named because he was a twin of his full brother al-ʿĪṣ; he came after him in birth and followed him (ʿaqabahu) in coming out.. It is also said that it is foreign and has no derivation.
(إسماعيل): a foreign proper name; its plurals are سماعلة, سماعيل and أساميع.
(إسحاق): a foreign proper name.

safi-cedvel:235-235.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) a conjunction; (لا جناح عليكم) its i'rab has passed [Note: In ayah 233 of this sūra.]; (في) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of lā [Note: Or it is a maṣdar-forming particle, and the interpreted maṣdar (ما عرّضتم) is in the position of genitive by the preposition, attached to the omitted khabar of lā.]; (عرّضتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and its fāʿil (agent); (الباء) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (عرّضتم); (من خطبة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in (به); (النساء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (أو) a conjunction, which may bear many meanings, among them permission, choice or distinguishing; (أكننتم) like عرّضتم; (في أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أكننتم), and (كم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (علم) a past verb; (الله) the word of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (كم) the noun of أنّ, in the position of accusative; (السين) a particle of the future; (تذكرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
The interpreted maṣdar from (أنّ), its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of علم.
(الواو) a conjunction; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) with no governing effect; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (تواعدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (سرّا) a second mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb), i.e. marriage [Note: Or it is a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl, with the object omitted, ألا [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a stray word] i.e. do not promise them marriage while concealing it; or it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, because it is its adjective, i.e. a secret promising.]; (إلّا) a particle of exception; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive-governing particle; (تقولوا) an imperfect verb, subjunctive, the sign of the subjunctive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقولوا) is in the position of accusative as the excepted [Note: It has been said: the exception is connected (muttaṣil), on the assumption that promising in a proper way is excepted from promising in general; this is what al-Zamakhsharī held. It has also been said: the exception is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because the proper saying is the indirect hint (taʿrīḍ), while that from which the exception is made is the explicit statement; this is the view of Abū Ḥayyān and those who followed him. Abū Ḥayyān said: This exception is disconnected, because it does not fall under (سرا) in His saying «ولكن لا تواعدوهنّ سرا», whichever interpretation you give it; and the proper saying is the hinting that has been permitted.. Then he says: This disconnected exception cannot have the governor before إلّا directed at it, because إلا means لكن, and the implied meaning is: but hinting is permissible.
So for the interpreted maṣdar, according to Abū Ḥayyān, only the accusative of exception is valid, as the grammatical rules establish, even if (إلا) is taken in the sense of لكن.]; (قولا) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (معروفا) a naʿt (adjective) of (قولا), accusative like it.
(الواو) a conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing; (تعزموا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (عقدة) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, because تعزموا is made to include the meaning of تنووا (intend) [Note: Or the meaning of توجبوا (make binding), or of تباشروا (undertake), or the meaning of any verb that is transitive by itself.. It has been said that عقدة is accusative as a maṣdar, and that the meaning of تعزموا is تعقدوا (conclude); and it has been said that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, the original being ولا تعزموا على عقدة النكاح.]; (النكاح) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يبلغ) an imperfect verb, subjunctive by a concealed (أن) after حتّى; (الكتاب) fāʿil, nominative; (أجل) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يبلغ) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تعزموا).
(الواو) resumptive; (اعلموا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the word of Majesty, the noun of أنّ, accusative; (يعلم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (ما) a relative noun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (في أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.
The interpreted maṣdar from (أنّ), its noun and its khabar stands in place of the two objects of اعلموا.
(الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (احذروا) like اعلموا, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) a conjunction; (اعلموا أنّ الله) like the first; (غفور) the khabar of أنّ, nominative; (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative. [Translator's note: so in the source; the ayah ends غَفُورٌ حَلِيمٌ, and the Morphology section below treats حليم.]
The clause لا جناح عليكم has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an earlier resumptive clause.
The clause عرّضتم has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the nominal or particle relative (ما).
The clause «أكننتم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause عرّضتم.
The clause «علم الله» has no grammatical position, being resumptive or parenthetical.
The clause «ستذكرونهنّ..» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «لا تواعدوهنّ..» is conjoined to something implied, i.e.: so mention them, but do not promise them.
The clause «تقولوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative.
The clause «لا تعزموا..» is conjoined to the clause لا تواعدوهنّ.
The clause «يبلغ الكتاب..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the concealed particle relative (أن).
The clause «اعلموا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعلم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of أنّ.
The clause احذروه has no grammatical position, being the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied condition, i.e. since Allah is aware of what is in your souls, beware of Him.
The clause اعلموا (the second) has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اعلموا (the first).

* Morphology:
(خطبة): a maṣdar meaning addressing a woman for marriage (proposal); here the maṣdar is annexed to its object, the original being: من خطبتكم النساء. It is with kasra on the khāʾ, like القعدة and الجلسة. It is taken either from الخطب, i.e. "matter", since it is one of the affairs (of life), or from الخطاب, since it is an exchange of address between the man and the woman.
(سرّا): a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the quadriliteral verb أسرّ; its pattern is فعل with kasra then sukūn; the regular maṣdar is إسرار.
(معروفا): a passive participle from عرف يعرف (category ضرب); its pattern is مفعول, i.e. what is known (acknowledged) by the Sharia (ayah 178).
(عقدة): the word is used here as a maṣdar, i.e. the contracting of marriage, so the maṣdar is annexed to its object. The pattern of عقدة is فعلة with ḍamma then sukūn; العقدة originally means the place of the knot.
(النكاح): a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb نكح ينكح المرأة (category ضرب and category فتح); its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(الكتاب): a noun meaning "that which is written", i.e. the prescribed waiting period; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ.
(حليم): one of the forms of intensification and of the ṣifa mushabbaha (adjective resembling the participle); here it is a ṣifa mushabbaha, so it is of the category كرم and indicates permanence and constancy (and see ayah 225).

* Rhetoric:
«وَلا جُناحَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِيما عَرَّضْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْ خِطْبَةِ النِّساءِ».
In the ayah there is a fine device, namely taʿrīḍ (allusion), which some include under kināya (metonymy).
If you say: What is the difference between kināya and taʿrīḍ? I say: kināya is to mention a thing by other than the word coined for it, as when you say "long of sword-belt and baldric" for tall stature, and "abundant in ashes" for a hospitable man. taʿrīḍ is to mention something by which you indicate something you have not mentioned, as when a needy person says to the one he needs: "I came to you to greet you and to look upon your noble face."
It is as though it inclines the speech to one side (ʿurḍ) that points to the aim; it is also called talwīḥ (hinting), because what he wants glimmers from it.

* Benefits:
1- taʿrīḍ is like a man's saying to the woman: "You are beautiful", or "righteous", or "beneficial", or his saying: "Perhaps Allah will make a righteous woman easy for me, for I wish to marry", and similar speech that suggests he wants to marry her, so that she keeps herself for him if she desires him, without his stating marriage to her explicitly.
2- خطب المرأة يخطبها خطبا and خطبة, with kasra; الخطيب is the suitor, and الخطب is the one who proposes to the woman; and she is his خطب whom he proposes to; the plural is أخطاب. رجل خطّاب: one who frequently goes about proposing. The poet said: برّح بالعينين خطّاب الكثب
تقول: إني خاطب، وقد كذب ... وإنما يخطب عشا من حلب
(The suitor of the milk-portions has tormented the eyes; he says "I am a suitor", and he has lied — he is only seeking a supper of milking.)
3- فاحذروه: the fāʾ is al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the "eloquent" fāʾ).
al-fāʾ al-faṣīḥa: it is the one where the thing conjoined to is omitted, though it is the cause of the conjoined, without assuming a conditional particle. It is called faṣīḥa because it discloses (tufṣiḥu) the omitted element and conveys an explanation of its cause.
Some said: it is the fāʾ that enters upon a clause caused by a clause not mentioned, as in the saying of the Exalted: «فَقُلْنَا اضْرِبْ بِعَصاكَ الْحَجَرَ فَانْفَجَرَتْ», i.e. he struck, and it gushed forth; and the saying of the Exalted: «لَوْ أَنَّ عِنْدَنا ذِكْراً مِنَ الْأَوَّلِينَ لَكُنَّا عِبادَ اللَّهِ الْمُخْلَصِينَ فَكَفَرُوا بِهِ», the implied meaning being:
then Muhammad came to them with the Reminder, and they disbelieved in it.

safi-cedvel:236-236.t:
* I'rab:
(لا جناح عليكم) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In ayah (233).]; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (طلقتم) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive.. and (تم) a pronoun, the fāʿil (agent); (النساء) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb); (ما) maṣdar-forming and temporal, containing the sense of a condition — or resembling a condition [Note: (ما) may be conditional, in which case the clause after it is parenthetical, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by the preceding speech.]; (لم) a particle of negation, jussive and inversion (to the past); (تمسّوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (ما لم تمسّوهنّ) is in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar (predicate) of lā.
(أو) a conjunction; (تفرضوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, conjoined to (تمسّوهنّ)..
and the wāw is the fāʿil [Note: The verb may be subjunctive by an obligatorily concealed (أن) after أو, which here means إلا; this is the view of al-Zamakhsharī, followed in it by Abū Ḥayyān and al-Bayḍāwī.]; (اللام) a preposition and (هنّ) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تفرضوا); (فريضة) a mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) a conjunction; (متّعوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هنّ) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (على الموسع) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted fronted khabar; (قدر) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) a conjunction; (على المقتر قدره) like the preceding phrase; (متاعا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it is a noun of maṣdar; (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (متاعا); (حقا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, confirming the content of the sentence; (على المحسنين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the implied verb حقّ, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ [Translator's note: the source has الباء (the bāʾ) here; the sign of the genitive in المحسنين is the yāʾ].
The clause «لا جناح عليكم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «إن طلّقتم..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: if you divorce women, there is no blame on you.
The clause «لم تمسّوهنّ» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The clause «تفرضوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause of the particle relative.
The clause «متّعوهنّ» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «على الموسع قدره» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of متّعوهنّ, the link being implied as منكم.. or it has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «على المقتر قدره» is in the position of accusative, or has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause على الموسع قدره.
The clause «(حقّ) ذلك حقا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(فريضة): a noun meaning "the thing prescribed", so it is فعيلة in the sense of مفعولة; or it is a maṣdar meaning prescribing.
(الموسع): an active participle from the intransitive (أوسع), i.e. he became possessed of ampleness and wealth, or from the transitive (أوسع), i.e.: أوسع النفقة, he made the spending abundant. In the word the hamza has been deleted; its original form is مؤوسع; the hamza was heavy, so it was deleted for lightening, and it became (موسع); its pattern is مفعل.
(قدره): maṣdar of قدر يقدر (category نصر and category ضرب); its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas, and its ʿayn may be made quiescent.
(المقتر): an active participle from the intransitive (أقتر), i.e. his wealth became little. In the word the hamza has been deleted; its original form is مؤقتر; the hamza was heavy, so it was deleted for lightening, and it became (مقتر); its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(متاعا): a noun of maṣdar from the quadriliteral verb متّع, whose regular maṣdar is تمتيع; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ (ayah 36).
(المحسنين): plural of المحسن, an active participle from the verb أحسن إليه and أحسن به, i.e. he gave him a good thing. In the word the hamza has been deleted for lightening, as happened in the word الموسع.

safi-cedvel:166-166.t:
* I'rab:
(إذ): an adverb for future time, a badal (substitute) of the first إذ in the previous verse. (تبرأ): a past verb. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (اتّبعوا): a passive past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma; the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). (من): a preposition. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تبرّأ). (اتّبعوا): a past verb and its fāʿil. (الواو): of the ḥāl (circumstantial). (رأوا): a past verb and its fāʿil. (العذاب): mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb). (الواو): conjunction. (تقطّع): a past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine. (الباء): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تقطّع); the bāʾ denotes passing away from (mujāwaza), in the sense of عن, or causation, i.e. "because of". (الأسباب): fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ).
The clause «تبرّأ الذين ... » is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct).
The clause «اتّبعوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of the first (الذين).
The clause «اتّبعوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the second (الذين).
The clause «رأوا» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of تبرأ, with قد implied «[Note: The clause may be conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause (تبرّأ), in the position of genitive.]».
The clause «تقطّعت بهم الأسباب» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause رأوا ... or in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause تبرّأ.

* Morphology:
(رأوا): it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, running along the lines of يرون «[Note: See verse (165) of this sūra.]».
(الأسباب): plural of سبب, a noun for what connects, literally and figuratively; its pattern is فعل with two fatḥas.

* Rhetoric:
- «وَتَقَطَّعَتْ بِهِمُ الْأَسْبابُ»: the original meaning of السبب is a rope in general, or the rope by which one reaches something, or the rope one of whose ends is attached to the roof, or the rope by which palm trees are climbed.. What is meant by «الأسباب» here is the bond that existed between the followers and the followed in this world, of kinship and affections, agreement in religion, following and seeking followers. This is by way of the unrestricted trope (al-majāz al-mursal).

safi-cedvel:167-167.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو): conjunction. (قال): a past verb. (الذين): a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as fāʿil (agent). (اتّبعوا): a past verb and its fāʿil. (لو): a particle of wishing that includes the sense of condition. (أنّ): a particle resembling the verb (of inna and its sisters), for emphasis. (اللام): a preposition. (نا): an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate) of anna. (كرة): the noun (ism) of anna, accusative (manṣūb).
The interpreted maṣdar from أنّ, its noun and its khabar is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ثبت", i.e. "if the occurrence of a return for us were established".. The apodosis (jawāb) of لو is omitted, its implied form being "لتبرّأنا".
(الفاء): the fāʾ of causation (al-sababiyya). (نتبرّأ): an imperfect verb, accusative by a concealed (أن) after the fāʾ; the accusative relies on the wishing with which لو is imbued. The fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "نحن".
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نتبرّأ) is in the position of nominative, conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, i.e. "if the occurrence of a return for us, and so our disowning them, were established".
(من): a preposition, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (نتبرّأ). (الكاف): a preposition and particle of comparison. (ما): a maṣdar-forming particle. (تبرّؤوا): a past verb, indeclinable on ḍamma; the wāw is the fāʿil. (منا): like منهم, attached to (تبرّؤوا).
The interpreted maṣdar from (ما) and the verb is in the position of genitive by the kāf, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of the verb نتبرّأ.
(الكاف): like the first. (ذا): a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq; (اللام) denotes distance and (الكاف) address.. i.e.
"He shows them a showing, or gathers them a gathering, or requites them a requital, like that". (يري): an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), the sign of its nominative being an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (الله): the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative. (أعمال): second mafʿūl bihi, accusative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (second term of the genitive construct). (حسرات): third mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of the accusative being the kasra «[Note: Or it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) if the seeing is considered visual.]». (عليهم): like منهم, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of حسرات «[Note: It may be attached to حسرات, because it is a noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar).]». (الواو): conjunction or of the ḥāl. (ما): negative, operating like laysa. (هم): a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as the noun of mā. (الباء): a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. (خارجين): genitive in form, accusative in position, the khabar of mā, the sign of the genitive being the bāʾ «[Translator's note: so in the source; the sign of the genitive is the yāʾ]». (من النار): a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خارجين).
The clause قال الذين اتّبعوا is in the position of genitive, conjoined to the clause تبرّأ in the previous verse.
The clause «اتّبعوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila (relative clause) of (الذين).
The clause «نتبرّأ» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the concealed particle relative (أن).
The clause «تبرّؤوا» has no grammatical position: ṣila of the particle relative (ما).
The object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is the clause "(ثبت) حصول الكرّة ...".
The clause «يريهم الله ... » has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ما هم بخارجين» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause يريهم الله.. or it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the object pronoun of يريهم.

* Morphology:
(كرّة): a maṣdar (verbal noun) of single occurrence (marra) of the verb كرّ يكرّ of the pattern-class of ضرب; its pattern is فعلة with fatḥa then sukūn.
