The clause «تبايعتم» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. The apodosis — if إذا is taken to contain the meaning of condition — is omitted, indicated by what precedes it, i.e.: when you trade, take witnesses.
The clause «لا يضارّ كاتب» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the resumptive clause.
(الواو) conjunction — or resumptive —; (إن) a conditional particle; (تفعلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الفاء) linking the apodosis; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis, and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of an accusative as the noun of إنّ; (فسوق) khabar, nominative; (الباء) a preposition, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted naʿt of فسوق; (الواو) resumptive; (اتّقوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الواو) resumptive; (يعلّم) an imperfect verb, nominative, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) the Name of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (بكلّ) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عليم; (شيء) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; and (عليم) khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن تفعلوا ...» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive or conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنه فسوق» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «اتّقوا الله» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «يعلّمكم الله» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.
The clause «الله ... عليم» has no grammatical position; it is resumptive.

* Morphology:
(دين): an aurally-transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar of the verb دان يدين, of the ضرب pattern; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(مسمّى): passive participle of the quadriliteral verb سمّى; its wazn is مفعّل, with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn.
(كاتب): active participle of the verb كتب; its wazn is فاعل.
(العدل): an aurally-transmitted maṣdar of the verb عدل; its wazn is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.
(يأب): it contains iʿlāl by deletion because of the jussive; its wazn is يفع.
(سفيها): a ṣifa mushabbaha (assimilated adjective) from سفه يسفه, of the فرح pattern; its wazn is فعيل.
(ترضون): it contains iʿlāl by deletion: the alif, the lām of the word, was deleted because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw was given a fatḥa to indicate the deleted alif; its wazn is تفعون, with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the ʿayn.
(إحداهما): the feminine of أحد, a noun used as a qualifier; the wazn of إحدى is فعلى, with kasra then sukūn.
(الأخرى): the feminine of الآخر, a derived adjective; its wazn is فعلى, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(دعوا): it contains iʿlāl by vowel-removal (taskīn) and iʿlāl by deletion; its original form is دعيوا, with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn; then the vowel of the yāʾ was moved to the ʿayn, and because of its quiescence and the quiescence of the plural wāw, the yāʾ was deleted, so the verb became دعوا, its wazn being فعوا, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and the ʿayn.
(صغيرا أو كبيرا): both are derived adjectives on the wazn فعيل, the first of the كرم pattern and the second of the فرح pattern and the كرم pattern (and see ayah 217).
(أقسط): an elative (ism tafḍīl) on the wazn أفعل; it is irregular because it is taken from the quadriliteral أقسط, meaning "he acted justly".
(أقوم): an elative on the wazn أفعل; it is either irregular, because it is from the quadriliteral أقام, or regular, taken from the triliteral قام. The wāw was not subjected to iʿlāl and changed to an alif as it was in the verb, because nouns are closer to fixity (jumūd) than verbs.
(أدنى): an elative on the wazn أفعل; it contains iʿlāl by substitution (qalb); its original form is أدنو, with fatḥa on the nūn; the wāw was changed to an alif because it is voweled and the letter before it has a fatḥa (see ayah 61 of this sūra).
(حاضرة): an active participle to which the tāʾ of the feminine has been joined; its wazn is فاعلة.

* Rhetoric:
1- «بدين»: it is mentioned to single out the intended sense of a shared (ambiguous) word and to remove the false impression explicitly, because تداينتم comes with the meaning "you dealt with one another by debt" and with the meaning "you requited one another". It cannot be objected that the context removes the ambiguity, because the discussion concerns explicit statement; moreover, the context may only be noticed by the perceptive. It is also mentioned so that the pronoun may refer back to it, for without it, it would have been said: فاكتبوا الدين (then write the debt).
2- «مسمى»: If you say: why did He say «إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى»? I say: so that it be known that the term must by right be known, such as fixing the time by the year, months and days. If one said: until the harvest, or الرياس [Translator's note: so in the text; perhaps a misprint for الدياس, "the threshing"], or the return of the pilgrims, it would not be permissible, for lack of specification.
3- «فليكتب»: that taught writing — He commanded it after prohibiting refusal of it, to emphasize it. And He took precaution for the matter by commanding him to fear Allah with His words: «وَلْيَتَّقِ اللَّهَ رَبَّهُ».
4- He repeated the Name of Majesty in the three clauses to instill awe and nurture reverence, and to draw attention to the independence of each of them with a meaning of its own: the first is an urging to piety, the second a promise of favour, and the third a glorification of His, the Exalted's, station.

safi-cedvel:188-188.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (لا) prohibitive, jussivizing; (تأكلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (أموال) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); (بين) an adverb of place, accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تأكلوا) «[Note: It is permissible to attach it to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of (أموالكم), i.e. present among you.]», (بالباطل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأكلوا) «[Note: I.e. do not take it by a false means. It is permissible for it to be attached to an omitted ḥāl of (أموالكم), i.e. extracted by falsehood, or to an omitted ḥāl of the fāʿil of تأكلوا, i.e. seeking the aid of falsehood.]», (الواو) the wāw of accompaniment (wāw al-maʿiyya); (تدلوا) an imperfect verb, accusative «[Note: It is permissible for it to be jussive by conjunction with (تأكلوا), with an omitted prohibitive (لا) understood, i.e. ولا تدلوا (and do not offer) ...]» by an (أن) necessarily implied (muḍmara) after the wāw of accompaniment, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الباء) a preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (تدلوا), (إلى الحكّام) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تدلوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تدلوا ...) is conjoined to a maṣdar cast from the content of the preceding speech, i.e.: let there not be an eating of wealth and an offering of it to the judges.
(اللام) causal (li-l-taʿlīl); (تأكلوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an (أن) implied after the lām ...
the wāw is the fāʿil; (فريقا) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من أموال) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of (فريقا), (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), (بالإثم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the pronoun in (تأكلوا), i.e. engaged in sin «[Note: It is permissible to attach it to an omitted ḥāl of (أموال الناس), or it is attached to (تأكلوا).]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأكلوا) is in the position of genitive by the lām, attached to (تدلوا), or to the verb of request: لا تأكلوا ...
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (أنتم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (تعلمون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ)..
And the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لا تأكلوا..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تدلوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.
The clause «تأكلوا فريقا..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «أنتم تعلمون» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
The clause «تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(الباطل), active participle from بطل يبطل on the pattern فاعل; then it was used as a noun meaning the opposite of truth.
(تدلوا), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is تدليوا, with ḍamma on the yāʾ: the ḍamma was deemed heavy on the yāʾ, so it was transferred to the letter before it; two vowelless letters met, so the yāʾ was deleted and the verb became تدلوا, its pattern being تفعوا.
(الحكّام), plural of الحاكم; originally an active participle from حكم يحكم, of the class of نصر, then it became a noun applied to one who judges between people; its pattern is فاعل.

* Benefits:
1- The lām of causation (lām al-taʿlīl) precedes the imperfect verb and it becomes accusative. The grammarians differed about the cause of the accusative, and they have two opinions on it: the first is that it is accusative by an أن optionally implied after the lām, and this is the opinion acted upon today and the opinion of the Basrans; the second, the opinion of the Kufans, is that the verb is accusative by a «كي» optionally implied after the lām. It appears that the first opinion is the preponderant one, «because the governing of «أن», overt and implied, optionally or necessarily, is widespread» «[Note: al-Naḥw al-Wāfī, vol. 4, p. 288..]».
2- Among the wonders of philology (fiqh al-lugha) is that letters on their own indicate meanings specific to them. Of this is that every verb whose fāʾ (first radical) is dāl and whose ʿayn (second radical) is lām indicates movement coupled with dangling down or slipping. Whoever would like more on the properties of letters should refer to the books of philology ...

safi-cedvel:189-189.t:
* I'rab:
(يسألون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (عن الأهلّة) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يسألون), (قل) an imperative verb, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "you" (أنت); (هي) a detached pronoun in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (مواقيت) khabar (predicate), nominative; (للناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of مواقيت; (الحج) conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الناس by the wāw, genitive like it; (الواو) conjunction; (ليس) a defective, rigid (jāmid) past verb; (البرّ) the noun of laysa, nominative; (الباء) a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تأتوا) an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (البيوت) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من ظهور) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تأتوا), since it is made to include the meaning of تدخلوا (enter), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تأتوا) is in the position of genitive by the redundant particle — this is the near position — and in the position of accusative as the khabar of laysa — this is the far position.
(الواو) conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) and accusative-governing; (البرّ) the noun of lākinna, accusative, and it is with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. ذا البرّ (the one possessing righteousness); (من) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as khabar; (اتّقى) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو), and it is the referent (al-ʿāʾid); (الواو) resumptive; (ائتوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (البيوت) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (من أبواب) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ائتوا), and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (اتّقوا) like ائتوا; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (لعلكم تفلحون) the i'rab of its like has preceded «[Note: In verse (185) of this sūra.]».
The clause «يسألونك..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being an explicative resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «هي مواقيت» is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «ليس البرّ بأن تأتوا» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause هي مواقيت «[Note: Or conjoined to the resumptive clause, in which case it has no grammatical position.]».
The clause «لكنّ البرّ من ...» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to the clause ليس البرّ.
The clause «اتّقى» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (من).
The clause «ائتوا البيوت» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اتّقوا الله» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause ائتوا البيوت.
The clause «لعلّكم تفلحون» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «تفلحون» is in the position of nominative as khabar of laʿalla.

* Morphology:
(الأهلّة), plural of هلال, a primitive (jāmid) noun. Its origin is أهللة — with sukūn on the hāʾ, kasra on the first lām and fatḥa on the second — then the first lām was made vowelless and its vowel transferred to the vowelless letter before it, and it was assimilated into the second lām. Its pattern is أفعلة.
(مواقيت), plural of ميقات. The word contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by qalb (conversion); its origin is موقات, with kasra on the mīm and sukūn on the wāw, because it is from الوقت (time). The wāw came vowelless after a kasra and was converted into a yāʾ; in the plural the wāw returned to its origin. The pattern of مواقيت is مفاعيل.
(الحجّ), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb حجّ يحجّ, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn; it may also occur with kasra on the fāʾ — as will come in verse (97) of Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
(تأتوا), it contains iʿlāl by deletion after iʿlāl by making vowelless. Its origin is تأتيوا, with ḍamma on the yāʾ: the ḍamma was deemed heavy on the yāʾ, so its vowel was transferred to the tāʾ and it was made vowelless; two vowelless letters met, so the yāʾ was deleted and it became تأتوا, its pattern being تفعوا.
(البيوت), plural of البيت, a primitive noun for a dwelling of hair, stone, clay or other material; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn. There is another plural, أبيات. The pattern of بيوت is فعول, with ḍamma on the fāʾ..
(ظهور), plural of ظهر, a primitive noun for the well-known body part (the back), and it has the form of a maṣdar; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.. The pattern of ظهور is فعول, with ḍamma on the fāʾ. There are two other plurals: أظهر, with ḍamma on the hāʾ, and ظهران, with ḍamma on the ẓāʾ (verse 101).
(اتّقى), it contains ibdāl (substitution) and iʿlāl. As for the ibdāl, it is in converting the fāʾ (first radical) of the word — which is the wāw — into a tāʾ because it came before the tāʾ of the iftiʿāl form; its origin is اوتقى. As for the iʿlāl, it is the conversion of the lām (third radical) of the word — which is the yāʾ — into an alif; its origin is اتّقي with fatḥa on the yāʾ: the yāʾ came vowelled after a fatḥa and was converted into an alif, and it became اتّقى. Its pattern is افتعل.
(وأتوا), the word has the deletion of the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) at its beginning because the wāw precedes it; its origin is ائتوا. When the wāw came, the connecting hamza was deleted, and the hamza was then written on an alif ... The word also contains iʿlāl by deletion, in the same way as تأتوا.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَلَيْسَ الْبِرُّ بِأَنْ تَأْتُوا الْبُيُوتَ مِنْ ظُهُورِها وَلكِنَّ الْبِرَّ مَنِ اتَّقى».
If you say: what is the connection of this speech with what precedes it?
I say: this is of digression (al-istiṭrād) in the Book of Allah the Exalted, and like it is His saying, Exalted is He: «وَما يَسْتَوِي الْبَحْرانِ هذا عَذْبٌ فُراتٌ سائِغٌ شَرابُهُ وَهذا مِلْحٌ أُجاجٌ وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ لَحْماً طَرِيًّا..» to the end of the verse. For He, Exalted is He, made clear the lack of equality between them up to His saying «أجاج», and with that the purpose of representing the lack of equality between the disbeliever and the Muslim was complete. Then His saying «وَمِنْ كُلٍّ تَأْكُلُونَ» does not establish the lack of equality; rather, what it conveys is their equality in what is mentioned. So it is of Allah's conducting speech by way of the aforementioned digression.

* Benefits:
1- In this verse and the verses that follow it, the Muslims' questions multiply about matters that touch their religion and that are of the essence of their new life. They ask their Messenger about the new moons: what is their nature? Why does the moon appear as a crescent, then grow until it rounds into a full moon, then begin to wane until it disappears? Then they ask him what they should spend, and about the amount they should spend; they ask him about fighting in the sacred month and at the Sacred Mosque; they ask him about wine and gambling and the ruling on them; and they ask him about menstruation and about the relations of men with women during that period.
These questions indicate the opening of thought and the awakening of religious sensibility, just as they have a historical significance regarding the development of the call and the obstacles it faced.
2- In this verse and the verses following it, you notice those purposeful closing comments that are closely related to the subject of the verse and remind of the fear of Allah: «وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ» «إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يُحِبُّ الْمُعْتَدِينَ» «وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الْمُتَّقِينَ» «وَأَحْسِنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحِبُّ الْمُحْسِنِينَ» «وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ الْعِقابِ» «وَتَزَوَّدُوا فَإِنَّ خَيْرَ الزَّادِ التَّقْوى» «وَاتَّقُونِ يا أُولِي الْأَلْبابِ»
These closing comments are closely bound up with the rites of worship, the feelings of the heart and the regulatory legislation, and this is a constant characteristic among the characteristics of the Noble Qur'an.

safi-cedvel:256-256.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) the lā of generic negation; (إكراه) the noun of لا, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of an accusative; (في الدين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of لا; (قد) particle of realisation (taḥqīq); (تبيّن) past verb; (الرشد) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (من الغيّ) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (تبيّن), by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of تميّز (to be distinguished); (الفاء) conjunction, of consequence (tafrīʿiyya); (من) a jussive conditional noun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (يكفر) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; (بالطاغوت) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يكفر); (الواو) conjunction; (يؤمن) like يكفر, and conjoined to it; (بالله) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤمن); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (قد) particle of realisation; (استمسك) like تبيّن, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; (بالعروة) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (استمسك); (الوثقى) naʿt (adjective) of العروة, genitive like it, and the sign of the genitive is the implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (انفصام) like إكراه; (اللام) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of لا; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (سميع) khabar, nominative; (عليم) second khabar, nominative.
The clause «لا إكراه في الدين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «قد تبين الرشد» has no grammatical position: causal.
The clause «من يكفر» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause تبيّن.
The clause «يكفر» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (من).
The clause «يؤمن» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause يكفر.
The clause «قد استمسك» is in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ) of the jussive condition, joined with the fāʾ. «[Translator's note: so in the source; this clause is in fact the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), as the author's own description of the fāʾ above indicates.]»
The clause «لا انفصام لها» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of العروة.
The clause «الله سميع» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(إكراه): maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb أكره; its pattern is إفعال.
(الرشد): maṣdar of رشد يرشد, of the bāb نصر; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn. And الرشد with two fatḥas is the maṣdar of رشد يرشد, of the bāb فرح يفرح; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.
(الغيّ): it contains a weak-letter change by substitution (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its origin is الغوي, with sukūn on the wāw. The wāw came with sukūn followed by the yāʾ, so the wāw was changed into a yāʾ and assimilated into the second yāʾ. Its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn, and it is the maṣdar of غوي يغوي.
(الطّاغوت): originally a maṣdar, like ملكوت. It is from the verb طغا يطغو (with wāw), or from طغى يطغى (with yāʾ); the tāʾ in it is additional. It contains a transposition (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr) and a weak-letter change by substitution: the lām of the word was moved before its ʿayn, so it became طوغوت or طيغوت; the weak letter had a vowel and the letter before it had fatḥa, so it was changed into an alif, and it became طاغوت. Its pattern is فلعوت.
Some take the tāʾ as substituted for the lām of the word — i.e. not additional — so there is no transposition and no weak-letter change; its pattern is then فاعول.
(العروة): originally the place where the hand grips. The basic sense of the root denotes attachment; from it comes عروته, when you come to him attaching yourself to him, and from it comes اعتراه الهمّ, i.e. worry attached itself to him. The pattern of العروة is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn.
(الوثقى): feminine of الأوثق, an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) bearing the article (ال), so it must agree with what precedes it in being feminine; its pattern is فعلى, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.
(انفصام): maṣdar of انفصم, a five-letter verb beginning with a connecting hamza (hamzat waṣl); its maṣdar comes on the pattern of its past form, with kasra on the third letter and an alif added before the last; its pattern is انفعال.

* Rhetoric:
In «العروة» there is an explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya), and «استمسك» is a reinforcement (tarshīḥ) of it, or another, dependent metaphor (istiʿāra tabaʿiyya). The utterance may also be taken as an allegory (tamthīl) built on likening the intellectual image drawn from holding fast to the truth — which admits no contradiction in any way at all, since it is established by clear, decisive proofs — to the sensory image drawn from holding on to a firm rope whose breaking is not to be feared.

safi-cedvel:257-257.t:
* I'rab:
(الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (وليّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (الذين) a relative noun in the position of a genitive «[Translator's note: the source has the typo جرف for جرّ.]» as muḍāf ilayhi; (آمنوا) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (يخرج) imperfect verb, nominative, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he"; (من الظلمات) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يخرج); (إلى النور) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخرج); (الواو) conjunction; (الذين) like the first, a mubtadaʾ in the position of a nominative; (كفروا) like آمنوا; (أولياء) mubtadaʾ, nominative, and (هم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الطاغوت) khabar, nominative; (يخرجون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the retention of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (من النور) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخرج); (إلى الظلمات) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يخرج); (أولاء) a demonstrative, indeclinable on the kasra, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ, and (الكاف) a particle of address; (أصحاب) khabar, nominative; (النار) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (هم) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (في) preposition and (ها) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (خالدون), which is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ هم, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the wāw.
The clause «الله وليّ ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «آمنوا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the first relative (الذين).
The clause «يخرجهم» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil or of the object.
The clause «الذين كفروا..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كفروا» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «أولياؤهم الطاغوت» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «يخرجونهم» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of the mubtadaʾ or the khabar ...
or it has no grammatical position, as an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أولئك أصحاب» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «هم فيها خالدون» is in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl of أصحاب النار «[Note: Or in the position of a nominative as a second khabar of the demonstrative mubtadaʾ أولئك.]».

* Morphology:
(وليّ): a ṣifa mushabbaha (resembling adjective) from the verb ولي يلي, of the bāb وثق; its pattern is فعيل. The yāʾ of فعيل met the lām of the word, so it was doubled. Its plural is أولياء (see verse 107 of this sūra).
(الظلمات): plural of الظلمة, a noun meaning the departure of light, derived from ظلم يظلم الليل (the night became dark), of the bāb فرح. The pattern of الظلمة is فعلة, with ḍamma then sukūn. There is another plural of ظلمة: ظلم, with ḍamma then fatḥa; and ظلمات with ḍamma then sukūn, and ظلمات with ḍamma then fatḥa (see verse 17 of this sūra).
(النور): the noun from نار ينور الشيء, of the bāb نصر, and it is light; its pattern is فعل, with ḍamma then sukūn; its plurals are أنوار and نيران.

* Rhetoric:
1- The singular النور is for the oneness of the truth, just as the plural الظلمات is for the multiplicity of the kinds of misguidance. This is a wonderful rhetorical secret.
2- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in borrowing الظلمات (darkness) and النور (light) for misguidance and guidance.
- If you ask: how do they bring the disbelievers out of the light, when they were never in light?
I reply: this is a wonderful device among the devices of rhetoric, namely negating a thing by affirming it. Its gist is that the speaker affirms something in his words and negates figuratively what is from its cause, while what is negated in the inner sense of the words is in reality what he affirmed.

safi-cedvel:258-258.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation expressing wonder (al-istifhām al-taʿajjubī); (لم) a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (تر) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "you" «[Note: The verb (ترى) here means "your knowledge reaches to".. and for this reason it is made transitive by (إلى).]»; (إلى) preposition; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ترى), and in the utterance there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the story of the one who disputed.."; (حاجّ) past verb, and its fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; (إبراهيم) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), barred from tanwīn because it is a proper name and foreign; (في ربّ) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (حاجّ), and (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi «[Note: The pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm or to the disputer.]»; (أن) a maṣdar-forming particle; (آتى) past verb, indeclinable on the implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif; (الله) the Divine Name, fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الملك) second mafʿūl bihi, and (الهاء) first mafʿūl bihi.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن آتاه الله ...) is in the position of a genitive governed by an omitted preposition, i.e. "because Allah had given him.." — so it has the sense of a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), attached to (حاجّ).. (إذ) an adverb of past time, in the position of an accusative, attached to the verb حاجّ; (قال) past verb; (إبراهيم) fāʿil, nominative, barred from tanwīn because it is a proper name and foreign; (ربّ) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the bāʾ, its appearance prevented by the place being occupied by the vowel suited [to the yāʾ], and (الياء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الذي) like the first, in the position of a nominative as khabar (predicate); (يحيي) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (الواو) conjunction; (يميت) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is "he". (قال) like the first, and the fāʿil refers to the disputer; (أنا) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ; (أحيي) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "I"; (الواو) conjunction; (أميت) like أحيي; (قال إبراهيم) like the first; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "If you claim that you are able, then Allah...". (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Divine Name, the noun of إنّ, accusative; (يأتي) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; (بالشمس) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي); (من المشرق) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يأتي) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الشمس.]»; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition; (ائت) imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the weak letter, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "you"; (الباء) preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (ائت); (من المغرب) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (ائت) «[Note: Or to an omitted ḥāl of the pronoun in (بها).]»; (الفاء) conjunction; (بهت) past verb in the passive form but with an active meaning «[Note: Or it is built for the passive and the relative is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).. and the omitted agent is Ibrāhīm, or it is the maṣdar understood from قال, i.e. Ibrāhīm's words bewildered him and confounded him ... This is the choice of Abū Ḥayyān.]»; (الذي) a relative noun, fāʿil; (كفر) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he". (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Divine Name, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (لا) negative; (يهدي) like يحيي; (القوم) mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (الظالمين) naʿt (adjective) of القوم, accusative like it, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ.
The clause «ألم تر..» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «حاجّ» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذي).
The clause «أتاه الله الملك» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the particle relative أن.
The clause «قال إبراهيم» is in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «ربّي الذي يحيي» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «يحيي» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the second relative (الذي).
The clause «يميت» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يحيي.
The clause «قال» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «أنا أحيي» is in the position of an accusative as the speech reported.
The clause «أحيي» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ أنا.
The clause «أميت» is in the position of a nominative, conjoined to the clause أحيي.
The clause «قال إبراهيم» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إنّ الله يأتي..» is the apodosis of an implied condition.
The clause «الشرط [the conditional clause] is the speech reported. «[Translator's note: so in the source, with the quotation unclosed; it means the implied conditional sentence is in the position of an accusative as maqūl al-qawl.]»
The clause «يأتي بالشمس..» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of إنّ.
The clause «ائت بها من المغرب» is in the position of a jussive as the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "If you are able, then bring it."
The clause «بهت الذي..» has no grammatical position, conjoined to the last resumptive clause.
The clause «كفر» has no grammatical position: the ṣila of the third relative (الذي).
The clause «الله لا يهدي ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive..
The clause «لا يهدي ...» is in the position of a nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).

* Morphology:
(فأت): the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) was dropped from the verb because the fāʾ entered on it; its origin is ائت. It also contains a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf): the lām of the word was dropped for the indeclinable [imperative] form. Its pattern is ففع, with sukūn on the second fāʾ (verse 106 and verse 222).
(المشرق): noun of place from the verb شرق يشرق, of the bāb نصر. By analogy it should have been مشرق with fatḥa on the rāʾ, because the ʿayn of the imperfect has ḍamma, but it came on مفعل with kasra on the ʿayn, and it is one of the irregular forms (shawādhdh) (see verse 115).
(المغرب): noun of place from the verb غرب يغرب, of the bāb نصر. It came irregularly on مفعل with kasra on the ʿayn, while by analogy it should have been on مفعل with fatḥa on the ʿayn.. (See verse 115.)
(بهت): in the passive form, while in its meaning it is active and requires a fāʿil. Like it in the Qur'an is هرع in the imperfect: «وجاءه قومه يهرعون إليه ...» [Hūd: 78].

safi-cedvel:214-214.t:
* I'rab:
(أم) the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, in the sense of "rather" (بل) plus the hamza; (حسب) past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, and (التاء) is the fāʿil (agent), and the mīm is a particle for the masculine plural; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تدخلوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (الجنّة) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تدخلوا ...) takes the place of the two objects of حسب [Note: According to the opinion of Sībawayh; and it takes the place of the first object, while the second object is omitted — according to the opinion of al-Akhfas [Translator's note: so in the source; al-Akhfash is meant.] — the implied form being "or did you think entering Paradise assured?"].
(الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لمّا) a particle of negation, conversion (to past meaning) and jussive; (يأت) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (مثل) fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ); (الذين) a relative noun in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (خلوا) past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif that was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters..
and the wāw is the fāʿil; (من قبل) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (خلوا), and (كم) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi..; (مسّ) past verb, and (التاء) the tāʾ of the feminine, and (هم) an attached pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; (البأساء) fāʿil, nominative; (الضرّاء) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to البأساء by the wāw, nominative like it; (الواو) conjunction; (زلزل) passive past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يقول) imperfect verb, accusative by (أن) necessarily implied after حتّى; (الرسول) fāʿil, nominative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقول) is in the position of genitive (majrūr) by (حتّى), and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (زلزلوا).
(الواو) conjunction; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative, conjoined to الرسول; (آمنوا) past verb and its fāʿil; (مع) adverb of place, accusative, attached to (آمنوا) [Note: It may be attached to (يقول), i.e. "they say along with the Messenger ..."]; (الهاء) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (متى) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) placed first; (نصر) postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative; (الله) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (ألا) a particle of alerting; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (نصر) the noun of inna, accusative; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قريب) the khabar of inna, nominative.
The clause «حسبتم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «تدخلوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).
The clause «لمّا يأتكم مثل..» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «خلوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «مسّتهم البأساء» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) or explicative.
The clause «زلزلوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause مسّتهم البأساء.
The clause «يقول الرسول» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «آمنوا معه» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the second relative (الذين).
The clause «متى نصر الله» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb "say" (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «إنّ نصر الله قريب» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption answering the question.

* Morphology:
(الجنّة): an underived (jāmid) noun meaning "garden"; it was so called because it is from (جنّ) meaning "to cover", as though the place were covered from others by its trees and shades; what is meant by the word here is the Garden of the Hereafter (see ayah 25 of this sūra).
(يأتكم): it contains a change (iʿlāl) by deletion because of the jussive: the yāʾ was dropped from it; its wazn is يفعكم.
(خلوا): it contains an iʿlāl by deletion: the third radical (lām) of the word, which is the alif, was dropped because it came quiescent before the quiescent wāw of the plural, and what precedes it was left with fatḥa to indicate the dropped alif; its wazn is فعوا with fatḥa on the ʿayn (ayah 14).
(البأساء والضرّاء): the hamza in both is extra, for the feminine.. see ayah 177 of this sūra.
(نصر): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb نصر ينصر (the first pattern); its wazn is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Benefits:
Ibn Jinnī pointed out in the book «al-Khaṣāʾiṣ» that strength of wording indicates strength of meaning. He established that when a word is on one pattern and then moves to a pattern larger in wording than the first, the new wording must contain more meaning than the meaning of the first wording. He gave as an example the verb اخشوشن, whose meaning is stronger than the verb خشن, and likewise: زلزل, وسوس, عسعس, etc.

safi-cedvel:215-215.t:
* I'rab:
(يسألون) imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (الكاف) a pronoun in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (ما) an interrogative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (ذا) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) [Note: (ماذا) may be parsed by making it one word: an interrogative noun, indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi placed first, its governor being ينفقون.. and the clause is the second object of the verb سأل, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative (ماذا), because asking is a cause of knowledge]; (ينفقون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil; (قل) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "أنت" (you); (ما) a conditional noun that makes the verb jussive, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as a mafʿūl bihi placed first, its governor being (أنفقتم), which is a past verb indeclinable on the sukūn, and the tāʾ is the fāʿil, and the mīm is a particle for the masculine plural, and the verb is in the position of jussive (majzūm) as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); (من خير) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of ما, or it is a tamyīz (specification) of ما; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (للوالدين) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "its destination" or "its place of spending is for the parents"; (الأقربين، اليتامى، المساكين، ابن) words conjoined to الوالدين by conjunctions, so they are genitive (majrūr) like it, the sign of the genitive being, respectively, the yāʾ, the kasra implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the overt kasra; (السبيل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (الواو) conjunction; (ما تفعلوا من خير) like ما أنفقتم من خير, and the verb in it is jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna; (الباء) preposition; (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (عليم), which is the khabar of inna, nominative.
The clause «يسألونك» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «ماذا..» is in the position of accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi, asking about a matter being treated as knowing it.
The clause «ينفقون» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (ذا).
The clause «قل ...» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «ما أنفقتم» is in the position of accusative as the speech reported by the verb "say" (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «(مآله) للوالدين» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined to the fāʾ.
The clause «إنّ الله به عليم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis of the second condition, joined to the fāʾ.

* Morphology:
(اليتامى): plural of اليتيم, a noun for one who lost one or both parents while young; its wazn is فعيل, and the wazn of the plural is فعالى with fatḥa on the fāʾ (see ayah 83 of this sūra).

* Benefits:
1- It is good for us to point to this distinctive style with which many ayahs of this sūra are opened, namely the method of question and answer, which is one of the features of eloquence in the Noble Qur'an. Here is a set of questions followed by a set of answers:
a question about spending: its places, its amounts and the kind of wealth in which spending is done; a question about fighting in the sacred month; a question about wine and gambling; and a question about orphans. These questions have motives and causes, which the seeker of more can return to in their places in the books of tafsīr and the books of fiqh and legislation.
2- The i'rab of the conditional particles can be summarized as follows:
a- من, ما, مهما: they are in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi when the verb of the condition requires a mafʿūl bihi; but if it is intransitive, or transitive having taken its object or two objects in full, they are in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
b- حيثما is in the position of accusative as an adverb of place.
c- متى, أيان, أين, أنى are in the position of accusative as an adverb of time. [Translator's note: so in the source; أين and أنّى are usually classed as adverbs of place.]
d- كيفما is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl of the fāʿil of the condition.
e- أي according to what it is annexed to.

safi-cedvel:216-216.t:
* I'rab:
(كتب) passive past verb; (على) preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive (majrūr), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (كتب) by its implying the meaning of "made obligatory"; (القتال) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هو) a detached pronoun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (كره) khabar (predicate), nominative; (اللام) preposition; (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (كره); (الواو) resumptive; (عسى) a complete (tāmm), inflexible (jāmid) past verb; (أن) a maṣdar-forming and accusative-governing particle; (تكرهوا) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (شيئا) mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative; (الواو) circumstantial; (هو خير لكم) like هو كره لكم; (الواو) conjunction; (عسى أن تحبّوا شيئا وهو شرّ لكم) the i'rab of its counterpart has already been given. (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ, nominative; (يعلم) imperfect verb, nominative, and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو" (He); (الواو) conjunction; (أنتم) a detached pronoun, indeclinable, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ; (لا) negative; (تعلمون) imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «كتب عليكم القتال» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «هو كره لكم» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «عسى أن تكرهوا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تكرهوا..) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of ʿasā.
The clause «هو خير لكم» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of (شيئا); its being indefinite is of no account because of the presence of the link (rābiṭ), which is the wāw.
The clause «عسى أن تحبّوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause عسى أن تكرهوا.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تحبّوا ...) is in the position of nominative as the fāʿil of the second ʿasā.
The clause «هو شرّ لكم» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl of the second (شيئا).
The clause «الله يعلم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يعلم» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الله).
The clause «أنتم لا تعلمون» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause الله يعلم.
The clause «لا تعلمون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).

* Morphology:
(القتال): an aurally transmitted (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the quadriliteral verb قاتل. Its wazn is فعل with kasra on the fāʾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the pattern of القتال is فعال (fiʿāl).]; as for its regular (qiyāsī) maṣdar, it is المقاتلة.
(كره): an aurally transmitted maṣdar of the verb كره يكره, of the pattern (bāb) فرح; its wazn is فعل with ḍamma then sukūn; the maṣdar has come as an adjective meaning مكروه (disliked).
(عسى): it contains a change (iʿlāl) by substitution: the yāʾ was changed to alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa; its wazn is فعل with two fatḥas.
(خير): it may be a maṣdar of the triliteral خار يخير, and it may be an elative noun (ism tafḍīl) from which the hamza was dropped, while the comparative (من) with its genitive noun is implied.
(شرّ): it may be a maṣdar of the triliteral, and it may be an elative noun from which the hamza was dropped, while the comparative (من) with its genitive noun is implied.

* Rhetoric:
«وَاللَّهُ يَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَعْلَمُونَ», i.e. He knows what is good for you and what is bad for you; the object was omitted for concision (ījāz).
In the ayah there is antithesis (ṭibāq) between love and dislike and between good and evil.

* Benefits:
1- There is a question regarding His saying, the Exalted: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتالُ. The ayah took a general direction, like His saying, the Exalted: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الصِّيامُ, but the jurists detailed the content of the ayah and said: «If the enemy enters the land, it is an individual obligation (farḍ ʿayn), and if the enemy is still in its own land, fighting it is a communal obligation (farḍ kifāya)», according to need and what the state decides.
2- A difficulty arises for one who parses His saying, the Exalted, «وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ» or «وَهُوَ شَرٌّ لَكُمْ» as a circumstantial clause because it comes after the wāw, even though it is preceded by an indefinite noun and its due would be to be parsed as an adjective. To be rid of this difficulty, it is reported that the wāw enters the circumstantial clause just as it enters the adjectival clause, and al-Zamakhsharī permitted that on the basis of His saying, the Exalted: «وَما أَهْلَكْنا مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ إِلَّا وَلَها كِتابٌ مَعْلُومٌ».
3- عسى: a non-inflecting verb whose meaning is approximation by way of hope, and it is of three kinds:
The first: it is in the status of the incomplete kāna, so it needs a noun and a khabar, and the khabar is only a future verb accompanied by the accusative-governing أن. The Exalted said: «عَسى رَبُّكُمْ أَنْ يَرْحَمَكُمْ», «فَعَسَى اللَّهُ أَنْ يَأْتِيَ بِالْفَتْحِ»: the Name of Majesty is the noun of ʿasā, and «أَنْ يَأْتِيَ», interpreted as a maṣdar, is the khabar of ʿasā. On this al-Farazdaq says, when he fled from al-Ḥajjāj after he threatened him with death:
وماذا عسى الحجاج يبلغ جهده ... إذا نحن جاوزنا حفير زياد
(And what might al-Ḥajjāj attain with all his effort, once we have passed beyond Ḥafīr Ziyād?)
Its khabar coming as a single word is anomalous, as in their saying in the proverb: «عسى الغريرا بؤسا» [Translator's note: so in the source; the proverb is usually cited as «عسى الغُوَيرُ أبؤسًا» ("perhaps the little cave holds misfortunes").].
The second: it is complete, as it is in this ayah: «عَسى أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئاً وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ».
The third: both preceding ways, the first and the second, are permitted with it, as in your saying: «عبد الله عسى أن يفلح», so we may make it incomplete, just as we may make it complete.
4- In this ayah there is one of the forms of correspondence (muqābala), which is a compound antithesis (ṭibāq); we find that in His saying, the Exalted: «أَنْ تَكْرَهُوا ... وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ، وأَنْ تُحِبُّوا ... هُوَ شَرٌّ».

safi-cedvel:240-240.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (الذين يتوفّون منكم ويذرون أزواجا) its i'rab has already been given [Note: In ayah (234) of this sūra.]; (وصيّة) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "يتركون وصيّة" (they leave a bequest) [Note: (وصيّة) may be a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being يوصون وصيّة (they bequeath a bequest), and the implied clause is the khabar of الذين.]; (لأزواج) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective) of وصيّة, and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (متاعا) a maṣdar in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. being provided for [Note: (غير) may be an adjective of متاع or a badal (substitute) of it, or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the maṣdar, having stood in for the verb, i.e.: لا إخراجا (without expulsion); this is the view of al-Akhfash.] [Translator's note: this footnote concerns غير and the next one concerns متاعا; they appear to have been swapped in the source]; (إلى الحول) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an adjective of متاع or to (متاعا); (غير) a ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb), of the wives or of the husbands, i.e. not being expelled (fem.) or not expelling (masc.) [Note: (متاعا) may be a mafʿūl bihi of an omitted verb, its implied form being يعطونهنّ (they give them), or a badal of وصيّة, or an adjective of وصيّة, or an accusative maṣdar (governed) by وصيّة, because (الوصيّة) has the meaning of يوصون, which means يمتّعون (they provide for).]; (إخراج) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr). (الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussive-governing conditional particle; (خرجن) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ)..
and (النون) the nūn of the feminine plural, the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) linking the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (لا جناح عليكم) its i'rab has passed [Note: See ayah (233) of this sūra and ayah (229).]; (في) a preposition; (ما) a relative noun in the position of genitive, attached to the khabar (predicate) of lā; (فعلن) like خرجن, and the fāʿil has no position [Translator's note: so in the source]; (في أنفس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (فعلن), and (هنّ) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (من معروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl of the implied referent pronoun, i.e. they did it of what is right; (الواو) resumptive; (الله) the word of Majesty, mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (عزيز) a khabar, nominative; (حكيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «الذين يتوفّون ...» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يتوفّون منكم..» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «يذرون ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «(يتركون) وصيّة» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (الذين).
The clause «إن خرجن» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا جناح عليكم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «فعلن» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (ما).
The clause «الله عزيز» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.

* Morphology:
(يتوفون): (see ayah 234, under Morphology).
(متاعا): a noun of maṣdar (ism maṣdar) of the verb متّع, whose regular maṣdar is تمتيع; and see ayah (236).

* Rhetoric:
majāz mursal (metonymic figure): in the saying of the Exalted «وَالَّذِينَ يُتَوَفَّوْنَ مِنْكُمْ وَيَذَرُونَ أَزْواجاً.
The woman whose husband has died is not called a wife after his death, because the marital bond ends with death; what is meant is the women who were wives to them. So the relation of the figure is consideration of what was.

* Benefits:
«غَيْرَ إِخْراجٍ»: in al-Kashshāf of al-Zamakhsharī three ways of parsing it are given: first, an emphatic maṣdar; second, a badal of «متاعا»; third, a ḥāl of the wives. All three ways are sound, but the last is the clearest and simplest.
This bequest was abrogated by the preceding ayah of waiting, and it was fixed at «four months and ten» («أربعة أشهر عشرا»).

safi-cedvel:241-241.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (للمطلّقات) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate); (متاع) a delayed mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (بالمعروف) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of متاع, or to متاع; (حقا) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "حقّ ذلك", so it confirms the content of the sentence before it; (على المتّقين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the implied verb حقّ.
The clause «للمطلّقات متاع» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «(حق) ذلك حقّا» has no grammatical position, being an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).

safi-cedvel:242-242.t:
* I'rab:
(الكاف) a preposition [Note: Or a noun meaning مثل, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and see ayah (187).]; (ذا) a demonstrative in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq, its implied form being "بيانا" (an explaining), and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) for address; (يبيّن) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); (الله) the word of Majesty, fāʿil (agent), nominative; (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يبيّن); (آيات) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of the accusative being the kasra, and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi; (لعلّ) a particle resembling the verb, expressing hope, and (كم) a pronoun in the position of accusative as the noun of لعلّ; (تعقلون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «يبيّن الله» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لعلّكم تعقلون» has no grammatical position, being causal (giving the reason).
The clause «تعقلون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of لعلّ.

safi-cedvel:243-243.t:
* I'rab:
(همزة) for interrogation, conveying alerting and wonder; (لم) a particle of negation, inversion (to the past) and jussive; (تر) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the weak letter [Note: The seeing here is of the heart (cognitive), and it should properly take two objects, but it has been made to include the meaning of "reaching", so it became transitive with the preposition إلى, i.e.: has your knowledge not reached such-and-such ... (al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ of Abū Ḥayyān, and the Ḥāshiya of al-Jamal on the Jalālayn).]; (إلى) a preposition; (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تر); (خرجوا) a past verb.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (من ديار) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (خرجوا), and (هم) an attached pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هم) a detached pronoun, mubtadaʾ (subject); (ألوف) a khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (حذر) a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), accusative (manṣūb); (الموت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr); (الفاء) a conjunction; (قال) a past verb; (اللام) a preposition and (هم) an attached (pronoun) in the position of genitive, attached to (قال); (الله) the word of Majesty, fāʿil, nominative; (موتوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (ثمّ) a conjunction; (أحيا) a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and (هم) a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو"; (أنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the word of Majesty, the noun of إنّ, accusative [Translator's note: the source writes the particle as أنّ here; in the ayah it is إنّ, as the clause list below has it]; (اللام) the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), conveying emphasis; (ذو) the khabar of إنّ, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw, for it is one of the five nouns [Note: Or the six, if الهن is added to them.]; (فضل) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (على الناس) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of فضل; (الواو) a conjunction; (لكنّ) a particle of rectification (istidrāk) governing the accusative; (أكثر) the noun of لكنّ, accusative; (الناس) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (لا) negating; (يشكرون) an imperfect verb, nominative.. and the wāw is the fāʿil.
The clause «لم تر إلى الذين..» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «خرجوا» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila of the relative (الذين).
The clause «هم ألوف» is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
The clause «قال لهم الله» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the ṣila clause.
The clause «موتوا» is in the position of accusative as the object of saying (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «أحياهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. so they died, then He gave them life.
The clause «إن الله لذو فضل» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لكنّ أكثر الناس..» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause إنّ الله لذو..
The clause «لا يشكرون» is in the position of nominative as the khabar of لكنّ.

* Morphology:
(تر): in it the hamza has been deleted for lightening; its original form is (ترأى) in the nominative state; and there is iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion on account of the jussive; its pattern is تف with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(أكثر): a derived adjective on the pattern أفعل meaning كثير (many), or it is in its original elative meaning, annexed to a definite noun. (See ayah 100 of this sūra.)

* Rhetoric:
1- «أَلَمْ تَرَ»: this expression may be said to one who already knows, and then it is for wonder, affirmation and reminding of one who knows what follows, such as the rabbis and the historians; and it may be said to one who is not so, and then it is to inform him and make him wonder. It has become so well known in this usage that it has been treated like a proverb in this field, by likening the state of one who has (not seen) the thing to the state of one who has seen it, in that it should not be hidden from him and that he ought to wonder at it. The seeing is either in the sense of eyesight, as a figure for looking, or in the sense of perception by the heart, including the meaning of reaching and arriving.
2- «حَذَرَ الْمَوْتِ»: what is meant is the plague that swept through them; this is a majāz mursal (metonymic figure), the relation being consideration of what this disease leads to.
3- In the ayah there is ṭibāq (antithesis) between causing death and giving life.
4- «فَقالَ لَهُمُ اللَّهُ مُوتُوا ثُمَّ أَحْياهُمْ».
That is: so they died, then He gave them life. It was omitted only to indicate that mentioning it is unnecessary, since it is impossible for what the Exalted intends to fail to follow His will. This is what is called in rhetoric concision by omission (al-ījāz bi-l-ḥadhf).

* Benefits:
1- This ayah begins with an affirmative interrogative (istifhām taqrīrī) accompanied by wonder and arousing of interest; what is meant by it is to arouse the listener's eagerness to know the substance of the story and to enjoy its moral..!
2- The hamza departs from real interrogation and comes for eight meanings:
a- Equalization (taswiya): it is the one that occurs after the word «سواء» or «ما أبالي» or «ما أدري» and «ليت شعري» and the like.
b- Refuting denial (al-inkār al-ibṭālī): it requires that what follows it — if the interrogation is removed — has not occurred and that the one who claims it is a liar, e.g. «أشهدوا خلقهم», «أَفَعَيِينا بِالْخَلْقِ الْأَوَّلِ», «أليس الله بكاف عبده».
c- Reproachful denial (al-inkār al-tawbīkhī): it requires that what follows it has occurred and that its doer is blameworthy, e.g.: «أَتَعْبُدُونَ ما تَنْحِتُونَ», «أَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ».
d- Affirmation (taqrīr): its meaning is your leading the addressee to admit and acknowledge a matter whose affirmation or negation is settled with him; you say: «أنصرت بكرا», «أبكرا نصرت».
e- Mockery (tahakkum): e.g. «قالُوا يا شُعَيْبُ أَصَلاتُكَ تَأْمُرُكَ أَنْ نَتْرُكَ ما يَعْبُدُ آباؤُنا».
And command (amr), e.g. «أَأَسْلَمْتُمْ», i.e. submit [Translator's note: the item letter (f) is missing in the source].
g- Wonder (taʿajjub): e.g.: «أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ». h- Finding slow (istibṭāʾ), e.g. «أَلَمْ يَأْنِ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوا أَنْ تَخْشَعَ قُلُوبُهُمْ لِذِكْرِ اللَّهِ».
3- It is said they were a people of the Children of Israel whose king called them to jihad, and they fled for fear of death, so Allah caused them to die for eight days, then gave them life..!!

safi-cedvel:190-190.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive; (قاتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (في سبيل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil of قاتلوا; (الله) the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable, in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (يقاتلون) an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussivizing; (تعتدوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb, for emphasis; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative (manṣūb); (لا) negative; (يحبّ) an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is a latent (mustatir) pronoun whose implied form is "he" (هو); (المعتدين) mafʿūl bihi, accusative, the sign of its accusative being the yāʾ.
The clause «قاتلوا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «يقاتلونكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative (الذين).
The clause «لا تعتدوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «إنّ الله..» has no grammatical position, being causal (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «لا يحبّ المعتدين» is in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of inna.

* Morphology:
(تعتدوا), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion, in the same way as تهتدوا.. see verse (137) of this sūra.
(المعتدين), plural of المعتدي, active participle from the five-letter اعتدى; its pattern is مفتعل.. It contains iʿlāl by deletion in the same way as المتّقين — see verse (2) of this sūra, Part One.

* Benefits:
1- الْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ is one of the many Quranic proverbs. Many of the eloquent words of the Qur'an have become proverbs, like His saying, Exalted is He, وَلَكُمْ فِي الْقِصاصِ حَياةٌ, and His saying: «إِنَّ اللَّهَ مَعَ الصَّابِرِينَ», and His saying: «وَلا تُلْقُوا بِأَيْدِيكُمْ إِلَى التَّهْلُكَةِ».
This is one of the fruits of Quranic eloquence, and how many are the aspects of eloquence in the Qur'an!
2- (حيث) is one of the adverbs of place that are permanently indeclinable even though they are in construct. Most often it is indeclinable on the ḍamma, and it is put in construct with nominal and verbal clauses, as in «قعدت حيث الجو معتدل (I sat where the weather is mild), وبقيت حيث طاب المقام (and I stayed where the abode was pleasant)». Rarely is it put in construct with a single word, and despite its rarity this is permissible; similarly its indicating time: they said that originally it is for place, but it may be for time, as in the poet's saying:
للفتى عقل يعيش به ... حيث تهدي ساقه قدمه
(The young man has a mind by which he lives, wherever his leg guides his foot.)
«i.e. حين تهدي (when it guides)».
Its being made genitive by the bāʾ is rare, as in «تلاقينا بحيث صافح أحدنا الآخر (we met where one of us shook hands with the other)», and likewise its being made genitive by the particle «الى», as in the poet's saying: «الى حيث ألقت رحلها أم قشعم» (to where Umm Qashʿam [death] cast down her saddle). Ibn Hishām said in al-Mughnī: mostly it is in the position of accusative as an adverb, or genitive by من, and it may be made genitive by other particles. It is best to adopt the opinion of Ibn Hishām because of the ease it offers..

safi-cedvel:191-191.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (اقتلوا) an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent), and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حيث) an adverb of place, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (اقتلوهم), (ثقفتم) a past verb and its fāʿil, and (الواو) a particle for prolonging the ḍamma on the mīm (ishbāʿ), and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) conjunction; (أخرجوهم) like اقتلوهم; (من) a preposition; (حيث) a noun, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of genitive, attached to (أخرجوهم), (أخرجوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الواو) parenthetical; (الفتنة) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); (أشدّ) khabar (predicate), nominative; (من القتل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to أشدّ; (الواو) conjunction; (لا) prohibitive, jussivizing; (تقاتلوا) an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), the sign of its jussive being the deletion of the nūn ... and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (عند) an adverb of place, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (تقاتلوهم), (المسجد) muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr); (الحرام) naʿt (adjective) of المسجد, genitive like it; (حتّى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (يقاتلوا) an imperfect verb, accusative by an (أن) implied (muḍmara) after حتّى, the sign of its accusative being the deletion of the nūn.. and the wāw is the fāʿil, and (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of genitive, attached to (يقاتلوا).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يقاتلوا) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (تقاتلوهم).
(الفاء) resumptive; (إن) a jussivizing particle of condition; (قاتلوا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma, in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil; (كم) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (اقتلوهم) like the first. (الكاف) a preposition of likening «[Note: Or a noun meaning مثل (like), in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is جزاء الكافرين.]», (ذا) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of genitive, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar, and (اللام) for distance and (الكاف) address; (جزاء) a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative; (الكافرين) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ.
The clause «اقتلوهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قاتلوا في سبيل الله «[Note: In verse (190) of this sūra.]».
The clause «ثقفتموهم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أخرجوهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اقتلوهم.
The clause «أخرجوكم» is in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «الفتنة أشدّ ...» has no grammatical position, being parenthetical.
The clause «لا تقاتلوهم» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause اقتلوهم حيث ...
The clause «يقاتلوكم» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle-relative (أن).
The clause «إن قاتلوكم» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «اقتلوهم» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis, joined with the fāʾ.
The clause «كذلك جزاء الكافرين» has no grammatical position, being resumptive and causal.

* Morphology:
(الفتنة), a heard (samāʿī) maṣdar (verbal noun) of the verb فتن يفتن, of the class of ضرب; its pattern is فعلة, with kasra on the fāʾ, on the pattern of the maṣdar of manner (maṣdar al-hayʾa).
(القتل), a heard maṣdar of the verb قتل يقتل, of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعل, with fatḥa then sukūn.

* Rhetoric:
1- «وَالْفِتْنَةُ أَشَدُّ مِنَ الْقَتْلِ», i.e. their idolatry in the Sanctuary is more abominable; or the trial by which a person is tried, such as expulsion from the homeland that sound natures love, is harder than killing, because its toil lasts and the soul suffers from it. On the first reading, the clause is of the kind of completion (al-takmīl) and precaution (al-iḥtirās) for His saying, Exalted is He: «وَاقْتُلُوهُمْ» etc., guarding against the impression that fighting in the Sanctuary is abominable, so how could it be commanded? On the second, it is a tailpiece (tadhyīl) to His saying, Glorified is He: «وَأَخْرِجُوهُمْ» etc., to show the nature of expulsion and to encourage it.

safi-cedvel:192-192.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) conjunction; (إن) a jussivizing particle of condition; (انتهوا) a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the alif deleted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, in the position of jussive as protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ).. and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); (الفاء) connecting the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); (إنّ) a particle resembling the verb; (الله) the Name of Majesty, the noun of inna, accusative; (غفور) the khabar (predicate) of inna, nominative (marfūʿ); (رحيم) a second khabar, nominative.
The clause «إن انتهوا» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قاتلوكم in the previous verse.
The clause «إنّ الله غفور» has no grammatical position, being a cause for the omitted apodosis,
i.e.: if they desist, then Allah forgives them, because Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

* Morphology:
(انتهوا), it contains iʿlāl (weak-letter change) by deletion; its origin is انتهاوا: the alif was deleted because it came vowelless before the vowelless wāw of the plural, and the letter before the wāw was given fatḥa as an indication of the deleted alif. Its pattern is افتعوا.

safi-cedvel:193-193.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) conjunction; (قاتلوا) its i'rab has preceded «[Note: In verse (190) of this sūra.]», and (هم) an attached pronoun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object); (حتى) a particle of limit and a preposition; (لا) negative; (تكون) a complete (tāmm) imperfect verb, accusative by an (أن) implied (muḍmara) after حتّى; (فتنة) fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
The interpreted maṣdar (ألّا تكون فتنة) is in the position of genitive by (حتّى), attached to (mutaʿalliq) (قاتلوهم).
(الواو) conjunction; (يكون) an imperfect verb, complete or defective, accusative, conjoined to the first تكون; (الدين) fāʿil, or the noun of يكون, nominative; (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial) of الدين, or to an omitted khabar (predicate) of يكون; (الفاء) resumptive; (إن انتهوا) its i'rab has preceded in the previous verse; (الفاء) connecting the apodosis; (لا) the lā of generic negation; (عدوان) the noun of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative; (إلّا) a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); (على الظالمين) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar of lā, the sign of the genitive being the yāʾ «[Note: It is permissible for the khabar to be omitted, i.e. لا عدوان على أحد (no hostility against anyone).. in which case (إلا) is a particle of exception and (على الظالمين) is a badal (substitute) of the khabar with the preposition repeated.]».
The clause «قاتلوهم ...» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause قاتلوا في سبيل الله or the clause اقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم «[Note: In verses (190, 191) of this sūra.]».
The clause «لا تكون فتنة» has no grammatical position, being the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-relative.
The clause «يكون الدين» has no grammatical position, being conjoined to the clause that is the ṣila of the particle-relative.
The clause «إن انتهوا» has no grammatical position, being resumptive.
The clause «لا عدوان إلا..» is in the position of jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), joined with the fāʾ..

* Morphology:
(عدوان), maṣdar (verbal noun) of عدا يعدو in the sense of اعتدى (transgressed), of the class of نصر; its pattern is فعلان, with ḍamma on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:259-259.t:
* I'rab:
(أو) conjunction; (الكاف) here a noun meaning مثل (like) «[Note: It may be in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, its implied form being "Have you seen the like of the one who ...". Al-Zamakhsharī allowed the kāf to be redundant (zāʾida), with the relative after it conjoined to the first relative in the previous verse.]», in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the first relative in the previous verse; the implied sense is: "Have you not considered the one who disputed with Ibrāhīm, or the like of the one who passed.."; (الذي) a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī), in the position of a genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; (مرّ) past verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, implied as "he", and it is the referent pronoun (ʿāʾid); (على قرية) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) (مرّ); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (هي) a detached pronoun in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject); (خاوية) khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ); (على عروش) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to خاوية «[Note: Or attached to an adjective of قرية, i.e. "a town existing (كائنة) upon its roofs", or "standing (ثابتة)".]», (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (قال) past verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "he"; (أنّى) meaning كيف (how), in the position of an accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of هذه «[Note: Al-ʿUkbarī allowed it to mean متى (when), so that it is an adverb of time in the position of an accusative, attached to (يحيي).]»; (يحيى) imperfect verb, nominative, and the sign of the nominative is the implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the yāʾ; (ها) a particle of alerting (tanbīh); (ذه) a demonstrative, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; (الله) fāʿil, nominative; (بعد) adverb of time, accusative (manṣūb), attached to (يحيي); (موت) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (ها) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi.. (الفاء) resumptive; (أمات) past verb, and (الهاء) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi; (الله) fāʿil, nominative; (مائة) adverb of time, accusative, attached to (أمات) by its being made to include (taḍmīn) the meaning of "He kept him dead for a hundred years"; (عام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (ثمّ) conjunction; (بعثه) like أماته, and the fāʿil is "He"; (قال) like the first, and the fāʿil is Allah; (كم) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (لبثت), which is a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (التاء) is the fāʿil; (قال) like the first, and the fāʿil refers to the one who passed; (لبثت) like the first; (يوما) mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), accusative, attached to (لبثت); (أو) conjunction; (بعض) maʿṭūf (conjoined) to (يوما), accusative like it; (يوم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; (قال) like the second; (بل) for inception and digression (iḍrāb); (لبثت مائة عام) like لبثت بعض يوم; (الفاء) linking the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "If you are not reassured, then look.."; (انظر) imperative verb, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "you"; (إلى الطعام) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (انظر), and (الكاف) a pronoun, muḍāf ilayhi; (الواو) conjunction; (شرابك) maʿṭūf to طعامك, genitive like it, plus muḍāf ilayhi; (لم) a particle of negation, conversion [to the past] and jussive; (يتسنّه) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "it" «[Note: It comes in the singular because it refers to two things taken as one thing, namely the concept of nourishment; or it refers to the drink alone, and the pronoun for the food is omitted because the second indicates it.]»; (الواو) conjunction; (انظر إلى حمارك) like انظر إلى طعامك; (الواو) conjunction; (اللام) the lām of causation; (نجعل) imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied (أن) after the lām, and (الكاف) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "we", for majesty; (آية) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative; (للناس) preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective) of آية.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نجعلك) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "We did that so that you may know, and so that We may make you a sign for people."
(الواو) conjunction; (انظر إلى العظام) like انظر إلى طعامك; (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable, in the position of an accusative as ḥāl; (ننشز) imperfect verb, nominative, and (ها) a pronoun, mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is a latent pronoun, implied as "we", for majesty; (ثم) conjunction; (نكسوها) like ننشزها; (لحما) second mafʿūl bihi, accusative.
